3046779_Jared Goff_DET.headline: Goff completed 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
3046779_Jared Goff_DET.story: The Lions surprisingly found themselves trailing throughout the majority of the second half, leading to Goff putting up season-high totals in all of completions, pass attempts and passing yards. The veteran signal-caller did see a three-game streak of multi-TD-pass tallies come to an end, with Sunday night's sole scoring strike going to Sam LaPorta from eight yards out late in the fourth quarter. Goff connected with seven different targets overall and helped facilitate Jameson Williams' first 100-yard effort of the season, but he'll now be tasked with trying to prevent Detroit from falling below .500 in a Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

4430737_Kyren Williams_LAR.headline: The Athletic's Nate Atkins believes the Rams will continue to use a backfield timeshare with Williams and Blake Corum this season.
4430737_Kyren Williams_LAR.story: Neither Williams nor Corum saw any action this preseason, as the Rams are notorious for resting their starters every summer, so it was difficult to get a clear picture of the backfield situation outside of practice. By all accounts, the Rams want to up Corum's usage after he saw double-digit touches once in the first six games of 2025, but seven times in the subsequent 11 regular-season contests. Working in Williams' favor, however, is coach Sean McVay's preference to use him near the goal line and on passing downs. Even with the talk of Corum getting more work, Williams appears to have a strong fantasy floor in one of the NFL's most potent offenses.

4360689_Tyler Shough_NO.headline: Shough (left hand) practiced in full Thursday.
4360689_Tyler Shough_NO.story: Shough was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough due to an injury to hie left, non-throwing hand, but it didn't impede him whatsoever one day later, indicating he's in the clear for Week 5 action. Through four games this season, he's taken advantage of a pass-heavy offense, completing 121 of 180 throws for 1,203 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions.

3916387_Lamar Jackson_BAL.headline: Jackson completed 21 of 31 passes for 235 yards and a touchdown and an interception while adding 34 rushing yards on four carries in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
3916387_Lamar Jackson_BAL.story: After throwing for 324 yards and averaging 13.0 yards per attempt in a win over the Colts last week, Jackson's passing numbers fell back to earth with Zay Flowers (hamstring) sidelined. The star QB still had a chance to put together a game-tying drive late in the fourth quarter, but Rashod Bateman broke off a route early and Jackson's pass attempt deep into New Orleans territory got intercepted instead. It was Jackson's first INT in two games, and he's amassed 559 passing yards and 74 rushing yards with three total TDs (two passing, one rushing) heading into a Week 3 road trip to Dallas.

4038815_Rico Dowdle_PIT.headline: Dowdle (toe) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
4038815_Rico Dowdle_PIT.story: Dowdle practiced for the second day in a row, albeit with a cap on his reps. Earlier Thursday, head coach Mike McCarthy told Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com that Dowdle's status for Sunday's game against the Colts is still up in the air, though the running back would put himself in good position to play this weekend if he's able to upgrade to full practice participation Friday. If Dowdle ultimately suits up versus the Colts, he'll likely be Option 1B in the backfield behind Jaylen Warren, who has averaged 6.5 yards per carry and 13.7 yards per reception over the past two weeks while Dowdle has been sidelined with a dislocated toe on his right foot.

3917792_Daniel Jones_IND.headline: Jones completed 19 of 34 passes for 143 yards and an interception in Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders. He added two yards and a rushing touchdown on four carries while committing a fumble.
3917792_Daniel Jones_IND.story: The two turnovers came in the first half, sandwiched around three possessions that ended in punts, but Jones settled down the rest of the way and put points on the board on six of the Colts' final seven drives. His fourth-quarter rushing TD was Jones' first of the year, but his 3:4 TD:INT remains poor, especially when combined when three lost fumbles in four games. He'll try to find some consistency and reduce his mistakes in Week 5 on the road in Pittsburgh.

3042519_Aaron Jones Sr._MIN.headline: Jones carried the ball 20 times for 94 yards and caught four of eight targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
3042519_Aaron Jones Sr._MIN.story: The Vikings' offense failed to produce a touchdown, but Jones got them into regular field-goal position as he set a new season high in scrimmage yards. The veteran RB has held up under a bell-cow workload while Jordan Mason (thumb) has been sidelined, averaging 23.0 touches over the last three weeks while still producing 4.3 yards per carry. Jones hasn't gotten into the end zone during that stretch, however, something he'll try to rectify in a Week 5 road trip to New Orleans.

4696981_Cam Skattebo_NYG.headline: Skattebo (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant at practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
4696981_Cam Skattebo_NYG.story: Skattebo has opened Week 5 prep with consecutive limited sessions. The top backfield option for the Giants will have one more opportunity Friday to upgrade to full participation as he looks to avoid carrying an injury designation into a game for the first time this season.

4360310_Trevor Lawrence_JAX.headline: Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions while adding three carries for no gain in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
4360310_Trevor Lawrence_JAX.story: While Lawrence saw opposite number Joe Burrow nearly double his passing production with a gaudy 428-yard total, the former guided his team to victory with a highly efficient and turnover-free effort. Lawrence averaged an impressive 9.9 yards per attempt and weathered a quartet of sacks while connecting with seven different targets. The 2021 first overall pick had to resort to relying heavily on tight end Brenton Strange (7-95-0 on eight targets), as Cincinnati effectively took away Lawrence's wide receivers for most of the afternoon, but the talented signal-caller did hit Brian Thomas from seven yards out in the second quarter for his one touchdown toss. Lawrence looks to be hitting on all cylinders to open his second season in Liam Coen's offense, taking a 69.2 percent completion rate, 843 passing yards and an 8:2 TD:INT into a Week 5 London showdown against the Eagles next Sunday.

3915511_Joe Burrow_CIN.headline: Burrow completed 39 of 54 passes for 428 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while rushing three times for six yards and another score in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also committed a fumble recovered by Cincinnati.
3915511_Joe Burrow_CIN.story: Burrow's passing yardage total was made all the more noteworthy by the fact he lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion in the first half. The prolific 2020 first-round pick put up new season highs in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, while also generating his first multi-interception tally of the campaign. The first of Burrow's picks came right after the two-minute warning in the first half at the Jaguars' 37-yard line and led to a Jacksonville touchdown. Nevertheless, he continued to battle as the Bengals trailed throughout the rest of the contest, and despite also losing Tee Higgins to an adductor injury with just under six minutes left, Burrow drove Cincinnati all the way down to the Jags' nine-yard line before losing the ball on downs with 56 seconds remaining. Prior to that point, Burrow had put his team in position for a potential game-winning touchdown via a 15-yard scoring toss to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter and a one-yard QB sneak with just over three minutes remaining for his first rushing score of the season. Burrow and the Bengals will look to regroup and potentially get Chase and Higgins back for a Week 5 road matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

4426338_Bo Nix_DEN.headline: Nix completed 22 of 31 passes for 288 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding five carries for six yards in the Broncos' 20-13 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
4426338_Bo Nix_DEN.story: Nix and the Broncos' offense started the game off in worrisome fashion, seemingly carrying over the malaise of their Week 1 Monday night loss to the Chiefs. Denver was still facing a 13-6 deficit heading into the fourth quarter, but Nix rallied the troops with a seven-yard touchdown pass to Nate Adkins and a key 17-yard strike to Evan Engram midway through the fourth quarter on what turned out to be the game-winning drive. The victory pulled the Broncos to 1-1 and gave Nix's early-season stats a serious boost heading into a Week 3 home showdown against the Rams next Sunday night.

4362921_Tyquan Thornton_KC.headline: Thornton is slated to undergo surgery later this week to address the dislocated left ankle he sustained in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders and is facing an expected recovery timeline of 3-to-4 months, Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com reports.
4362921_Tyquan Thornton_KC.story: Depending how quickly Thornton bounces back from surgery, Zenitz notes that the speedy receiver could have a small chance at returning late in the regular season or during the playoffs. The injury nonetheless is a devastating development for Thornton, who had turned in perhaps the best performance of his career -- a five-catch, 111-yard, two-touchdown effort on eight targets -- before going down with the gruesome ankle injury at the end of a 55-yard reception with just under four minutes left in the fourth quarter. In Thornton's absence, the Chiefs could call upon Xavier Worthy to run more vertical routes, and Kansas City also may have interest in a reunion with Tyreek Hill (knee), who is expected to sign a deal with a team within the next few days.

3116389_Samaje Perine_CIN.headline: Perine rushed three times for seven yards in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars.
3116389_Samaje Perine_CIN.story: Chase Brown carried the ball nine times for just 10 yards, and the Bengals rushed 15 times for just 23 yards as a team, with Joe Burrow scoring a rushing touchdown. Perine has rushed 13 times for 42 yards (3.2 YPC) through four games. He would need an injury to Brown to gain any fantasy relevance.

3929630_Saquon Barkley_PHI.headline: Barkley (stinger) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
3929630_Saquon Barkley_PHI.story: Barkley missed most of the first half of the Eagles' Week 2 win at Tennessee due to a stinger, but he returned in the second half and ended the contest with five touches for 20 yards from scrimmage. He told Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer on Thursday that an MRI on his left shoulder "went well," and during the corresponding session he was spotted wearing a protective device on his shoulder and neck area, per Zach Berman of The Athletic. Barkley is actually the healthiest of the running backs on Philadelphia's active roster, as both Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot) were held out of drills entirely to begin Week 3 prep. The overall situation bears monitoring in the coming days to see who among the trio will be available Monday in Chicago.

15864_Geno Smith_NYJ.headline: Smith completed eight of 15 pass attempts for 119 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
15864_Geno Smith_NYJ.story: Smith threw for just 18 yards in the first half as the Jets took a 13-3 deficit into the locker room. Things didn't get much better offensively after halftime, except for Smith's 58-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Williams in the fourth quarter. Smith has a 5:0 TD:INT and is averaging 226 passing yards heading into a Week 5 home game against the Browns.

2577417_Dak Prescott_DAL.headline: Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-30 win over the Texans. He added seven yards on two carries.
2577417_Dak Prescott_DAL.story: A surreal 21 of Prescott's 45 attempts went to CeeDee Lamb, and the duo connected on a 12-yard TD with just 40 seconds left in the game for the game-winning score after Javonte Williams had scored Dallas' first three touchdowns in the second half as part of a comeback from a 16-6 halftime deficit. The 335 passing yards (189 of them to Lamb) were a season high for Prescott, and he'll take an 8:1 TD:INT through four games into a Week 5 battle at home against the Buccaneers.

4361579_Javonte Williams_DAL.headline: Williams carried the ball 19 times for 62 yards and three touchdowns while catching all five of his targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 34-30 win over the Texans.
4361579_Javonte Williams_DAL.story: A 16-6 lead for Houston at the half transformed into a barn burner that saw Williams hit paydirt on three straight possessions to begin the second half, with his TD runs coming from eight, one and two yards out. The 26-year-old running back is proving his 2025 breakout was no fluke, and through four games to begin the current campaign he's scored six touchdowns (five on the ground, one through the air) while putting together 308 scrimmage yards. Williams will look to keep rolling in a Week 5 home tilt against the Buccaneers on Thursday.

4685720_Bryce Young_CAR.headline: Young completed 23 of 36 passes for 287 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and added one carry for six yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
4685720_Bryce Young_CAR.story: The Panthers weren't particularly threatened by the Falcons at any point Sunday, so Young's robust passing yardage total was particularly noteworthy in that context. The 2023 first overall pick posted a second straight three-touchdown performance to open the season, connecting with Chuba Hubbard (three yards) and Darren Waller (seven, 12 yards) for his trio of scoring tosses. Young hooked up with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and with 648 passing yards and six touchdowns versus one interception through the first pair of contests, he's clicking on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 road matchup against the Browns.

4430807_Bijan Robinson_ATL.headline: Robinson did not play in the Falcons' 27-7 preseason loss to the Broncos on Friday.
4430807_Bijan Robinson_ATL.story: Robinson dressed and warmed up pregame but observed Friday's exhibition contest from the sidelines. He was the only Falcons running back to not suit up, as Brian Robinson played in each of the first two offensive series while Tyler Goodson led all Atlanta RB's with 24 snaps on offense. Per Will McFadden and Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site, Robinson is still in ramp-up mode after recently returning to practice, so he could play in Atlanta's next preseason game, which takes place Saturday, Aug. 22, against Indianapolis.

4361741_Brock Purdy_SF.headline: Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins. He also rushed three times for 30 yards and a touchdown.
4361741_Brock Purdy_SF.story: Purdy was in complete command of the offense throughout Sunday's lopsided win, throwing only two incompletions while finishing as the team's leading rusher for the cherry on top. The 49ers have been one of the league's best teams in the early going, outscoring the Rams and Dolphins by a combined margin of 62-20 heading into a Week 3 home game against the Cardinals. Purdy has contributed six total touchdowns during this hot start, including third-quarter touchdown passes of 12 yards to George Kittle and six yards to Kyle Juszczyk against the Dolphins following Purdy's two-yard touchdown run in the second quarter.

4038941_Justin Herbert_LAC.headline: Herbert was 19-for-31 passing for 189 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, took six carries for 40 yards and lost a fumble during Sunday's 30-23 loss in Seattle.
4038941_Justin Herbert_LAC.story: Herbert's three turnovers led directly to seven points for the Seahawks -- i.e., L.A.'s margin of defeat -- and he didn't reach the 200-yard threshold through the air for the second time in four contests this season. Having Ladd McConkey at less than 100 percent didn't help matters, and the team's top wide receiver appeared to aggravate an existing foot injury in the second half and didn't return to action. Herbert boasts just four touchdown passes versus six interceptions in 2026, and he may find it difficult to achieve his first win of the campaign next Sunday against the Broncos.

4427095_DeMario Douglas_NE.headline: Douglas caught two of three targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 29-26 win over Buffalo.
4427095_DeMario Douglas_NE.story: Douglas didn't really make much of a splash in Week 4, but he was able to reel in multiple passes for the first time since Week 1. The wide receiver could step into a more prominent role beginning in Week 5 against the Raiders after Mack Hollins suffered a calf injury in Sunday's victory. Through four contests this season, Douglas has caught nine of 17 targets for 82 yards.

3045523_Kendrick Bourne_SF.headline: Bourne is slated to signed a two-year contract with the Cardinals, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
3045523_Kendrick Bourne_SF.story: Bourne's pending addition brings a more reliable No. 3 WR to Arizona than Greg Dortch, who is an unrestricted free agent. In 16 regular-season games in 2025, Bourne filled in nicely in a 49ers receiving corps beset by injuries, finishing with 37 catches (on 53 targets) for 551 yards and no touchdowns. Bourne will line up behind holdovers Marvin Harrison (foot) and Michael Wilson with the Cardinals.

8439_Aaron Rodgers_PIT.headline: Rodgers completed 22 of 40 passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday. He also ran in a game-tying two-point conversion.
8439_Aaron Rodgers_PIT.story: Rodgers' final line underscores the type of uneven night it was for the future Hall of Famer and the Steelers offense as a whole. He got started on the right foot by leading a marathon 17-play, 78-yard drive that consumed 9:48 on Pittsburgh's opening drive, one he capped off with a 12-yard touchdown shovel pass to Roman Wilson. Rodgers would go on to add 21- and three-yard scoring tosses in the fourth quarter to tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth, respectively, the latter which the 22-year veteran followed up with a game-tying two-point conversion quarterback sneak. However, Rodgers' one non-Hail Mary interception in the second quarter, which was largely the result of his arm being hit as he threw, did lead to a Cleveland touchdown. Rodgers, who now has consecutive three-touchdown tallies, will look to regroup over the extended time between Thursday and a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

4036378_Jordan Love_GB.headline: Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards with two touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for minus-8 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
4036378_Jordan Love_GB.story: Love's final line was a serviceable one despite the low-scoring and often choppy game, and the veteran signal-caller salvaged his fantasy day with touchdown tosses of two yards each to Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft. Love spread the ball around to eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and although he's completed a career-low 56.5 percent of his passes through four games, he also boasts an 8:3 TD:INT in that span. Love next takes on the division-rival Bears in a Week 5 home matchup next Sunday.

4430737_Kyren Williams_LA.headline: The Athletic's Nate Atkins believes the Rams will continue to use a backfield timeshare with Williams and Blake Corum this season.
4430737_Kyren Williams_LA.story: Neither Williams nor Corum saw any action this preseason, as the Rams are notorious for resting their starters every summer, so it was difficult to get a clear picture of the backfield situation outside of practice. By all accounts, the Rams want to up Corum's usage after he saw double-digit touches once in the first six games of 2025, but seven times in the subsequent 11 regular-season contests. Working in Williams' favor, however, is coach Sean McVay's preference to use him near the goal line and on passing downs. Even with the talk of Corum getting more work, Williams appears to have a strong fantasy floor in one of the NFL's most potent offenses.

3917315_Kyler Murray_MIN.headline: Murray completed 27 of 37 passes for 247 yards while adding 16 rushing yards on six carries in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
3917315_Kyler Murray_MIN.story: All of Minnesota's points came from the boot of Will Reichard, as Murray failed to lead the team into the end zone but also avoided committing any turnovers. With the defense playing at a high level, the veteran QB has been able to get away with a lack of production, but a 1:2 TD:INT through two-plus starts and little additional yardage on the ground may lead to some job security issues with Carson Wentz having proven he can run the offense effectively while Murray was sidelined with a concussion. The former Cardinal will try to find a rhythm during a Week 5 road trip to New Orleans.

4431452_Drake Maye_NE.headline: Maye completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding eight rushes for 54 yards in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday. He threw a two-point conversion pass and committed three fumbles, losing one and recovering the other two.
4431452_Drake Maye_NE.story: Maye's eclectic stat line was reflective of New England's topsy-turvy win, during which the Patriots overcame a 17-7 halftime deficit and recorded the game-winning touchdown with 1:50 remaining to seal the comeback victory. The previously embattled 2024 first-round pick's day started off in positive fashion with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Romeo Doubs to cap off New England's first possession, and he went back to Doubs from two yards out in the third quarter to bring New England within three. However, the Patriots were in danger of falling to 1-3 on the season when they found themselves down 26-21 as late as the two-minute warning, but Maye was able to connect with Efton Chism for a 23-yard scoring strike the young receiver snared with one hand down the right sideline with 1:50 remaining and then completed a two-point conversion pass to Rhamondre Stevenson. Maye's performance was a much-needed bounce-back effort after he went into the day having thrown for no more than 208 yards in any of his first three games while generating a 1:6 TD:INT. He'll look to carry over the momentum into a Week 5 home showdown against the surprisingly resurgent Raiders next Sunday.

3912547_Sam Darnold_SEA.headline: Darnold completed 13 of 22 passes for 168 yards, two touchdowns and one interception and rushed three times for six yards during Sunday's 30-23 victory against the Chargers.
3912547_Sam Darnold_SEA.story: On a day in which the Seahawks rode the ground game to the tune of 33 carries, led by RB Emanuel Wilson's 21, Darnold didn't have to do much to keep the Chargers at bay. Darnold's two touchdown throws went for 23 (Wilson) and six yards (WR Tory Horton), bringing his total on the campaign to six in a little more than eight quarters of play. Darnold will be seeking to bounce back in terms of yardage, at least, next Sunday versus the 49ers.

4683062_Xavier Worthy_KC.headline: Worthy caught four of seven targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
4683062_Xavier Worthy_KC.story: Worthy finished second on the team in targets and receiving yards behind Tyquan Thornton, who caught five of eight targets for 111 yards and two touchdowns prior to suffering an ankle injury in the fourth quarter. Rashee Rice (hamstring) exited the game in the first quarter, so Worthy is the top healthy wide receiver for Kansas City, though Rice will have a chance to heal during the Week 5 bye before the Chargers come to town in Week 6.

4808766_Mason Taylor_NYJ.headline: Taylor (thumb) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
4808766_Mason Taylor_NYJ.story: Taylor didn't practice in any fashion and sat out for both of the Jets' past two games due to the thumb injury, but he appears to be close to 100 percent ahead of Sunday's contest against the Browns after operating with no restrictions to kick off Week 5 prep. The second-year tight end paced Jets tight ends in snaps through the first two weeks of the season, but he may have to settle for a lesser role upon his return. Rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq -- who handled light workloads the first two weeks after missing much of training camp and the preseason while recovering from hernia surgery -- has seen his snap counts ramp up over the past two weeks while Taylor was sidelined and produced a 7-105-1 receiving line on 12 targets during that stretch. Sadiq now looks poised to operate as the Jets' top option at tight end ahead of Taylor moving forward.

4361432_Romeo Doubs_NE.headline: Doubs secured six of nine targets for 58 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday.
4361432_Romeo Doubs_NE.story: Doubs put together a performance befitting his current role as No. 1 receiver in the ongoing absence of A.J. Brown (ankle, IR), recording his first two touchdowns as a member of the Patriots while finishing as the team leader in receptions and targets with figures that also qualified as season highs. Doubs struck from 14 and two yards out in the first and third quarter, respectively, on his pair of scoring grabs, and after a blanking in Week 1 against Seattle, he's bounced back with a 12-203-2 line on 20 targets. Doubs will next try to make inroads against a tough Raiders defense at home in Week 5.

4360939_Rashod Bateman_BAL.headline: Bateman caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-17 loss to New Orleans.
4360939_Rashod Bateman_BAL.story: With Zay Flowers (hamstring) unavailable, Bateman stepped up as Lamar Jackson's top downfield option and hauled in a 22-yard TD just before halftime, giving the Ravens a 14-3 lead. The veteran wideout made a mental error that may have cost his team the game, however -- on Baltimore's final possession as the Ravens were looking to tie it up, he cut a route short and saw Jackson's pass attempt sail over his head for a game-ending interception. Flowers could be back as soon as next week, which would relegate Bateman to a supporting role again for a Week 3 road trip to Dallas.

3925357_Calvin Ridley_TEN.headline: Ridley caught one pass (on two targets) for 13 yards during Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Ravens.
3925357_Calvin Ridley_TEN.story: Ridley and the rest of the Titans pass catchers took a back seat to rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate, who turned 12 of his targets from Cam Ward into nine catches for 145 yards. Ridley was on the field for 30 of Tennessee's 64 offensive snaps, which was fewer than Tate (54), Wan'Dale Robinson (43) and Elic Ayomanor (40). Ridley is off to a slow start to the 2026 season, accumulating only three catches (on five targets) for 48 yards through four games. The Titans head home for Week 5 against the Texans, whose secondary was torched by CeeDee Lamb in a Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.

4430027_Sam LaPorta_DET.headline: LaPorta brought in eight of 13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
4430027_Sam LaPorta_DET.story: LaPorta turned in season-high numbers across all three components of his receiving line, and he added his second touchdown of the campaign on an eight-yard grab with 3:38 remaining to bring the Lions to within six points. LaPorta has had a steady role through the first four games of the season, netting a 22-228-2 line on 32 targets. It's worth noting many of LaPorta's receptions have had an impact, as he's produced 12 first downs and already has three catches of 20-plus yards heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

4686422_Xavier Hutchinson_HOU.headline: Hutchinson caught three of five targets for 46 yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
4686422_Xavier Hutchinson_HOU.story: With Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence, Hutchinson saw his snaps cut pretty significantly, as he was in on just 17 of Houston's 55 plays from scrimmage. He still saw five targets, but Hutchinson appears to be the biggest loser at wide receiver with Collins back in action and can be left on waivers in most fantasy formats.

4595348_Malik Nabers_NYG.headline: Nabers (knee) was listed as a limited participant at practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
4595348_Malik Nabers_NYG.story: Nabers returned to practice Thursday after sitting out Wednesday's session, but he isn't completely out of the woods yet. An upgrade to full participation Friday could help Nabers avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

4678006_Elijah Arroyo_SEA.headline: Arroyo secured his only target for a 24-yard reception in the Seahawks' 9-9 preseason tie with the Chiefs on Friday.
4678006_Elijah Arroyo_SEA.story: The second-year tight end had recorded a 36-yard touchdown grab in Sunday's exhibition against the Titans, and Arroyo followed that up with another big play Friday on his 24-yard grab during Seattle's second possession. Arroyo is expected to operate as the No. 2 pass-catching option at tight end behind AJ Barner, but veteran Eric Saubert is expected to see his fair share of snaps as well thanks to his blocking prowess.

4374302_Amon-Ra St. Brown_DET.headline: St. Brown secured eight of 11 targets for 75 yards in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
4374302_Amon-Ra St. Brown_DET.story: St. Brown was essentially as busy as usual in the air attack, although he was in the relatively rare position of finishing second in targets, and to tight end Sam LaPorta at that. Nevertheless, the star wideout tied with LaPorta for the team lead in receptions, and St. Brown's yardage tally was his second-highest figure through the first four games. Despite the disappointing team-level outcome, St. Brown's fantasy outlook is as bright as customary heading into a favorable Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

4432620_Parker Washington_JAX.headline: Washington secured one of three targets for seven yards, rushed once for three yards and returned one punt for three yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
4432620_Parker Washington_JAX.story: Washington had been Trevor Lawrence's top target by a comfortable margin over the first three games of the season, but the Bengals effectively shut down the bulk of Jacksonville's wide-receiver production Sunday. Washington saw the biggest downturn, making it a forgettable fantasy afternoon overall despite the team-level success the Jaguars enjoyed. Washington figures to have an uphill battle in terms of a potential Week 5 resurgence as well, considering the Jaguars will face off with a talented Eagles defense in a Week 5 matchup in London next Sunday.

4569618_Garrett Wilson_NYJ.headline: Wilson caught three of four targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
4569618_Garrett Wilson_NYJ.story: Wilson accounted for two of Geno Smith's three completions in the first half, and the star wide receiver finished with a team-high three catches as Smith completed only eight passes in a forgettable performance from New York's offense. Heading into Sunday's loss, Wilson had been averaging seven catches for 81 receiving yards per game. Wilson and the Jets will try to bounce back from this dud in Week 5 against the Browns.

4723086_Colston Loveland_CHI.headline: Loveland caught six of nine targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets.
4723086_Colston Loveland_CHI.story: Loveland led the team with nine targets, tying his total from the previous three games combined. The 2025 first-round pick has been trending in the right direction after a painfully slow start, increasing his yardage total from zero to three to 31 to 57 in the first four games of his second regular season. Considering that Loveland's best game of the season came Sunday in Tyson Bagent's first start of the campaign, Loveland probably wouldn't mind Bagent sticking in the starting role for Week 5 at Green Bay, though Caleb Williams (hamstring) will reprise the starting job once healthy.

4576297_AJ Barner_SEA.headline: Barner caught one of three targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
4576297_AJ Barner_SEA.story: Barner wasn't particularly busy in Week 4, garnering three or fewer targets for the third time this season. The tight end remains an unappealing fantasy option as the Seahawks' passing attack funnels through Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the rest of Seattle's pass catchers are just reaching for crumbs.

15847_Travis Kelce_KC.headline: Kelce caught two of four targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
15847_Travis Kelce_KC.story: Kelce was surprisingly quiet in this battle between AFC West rivals that both entered the game with 3-0 records. This was the second consecutive game in which Kelce was held to two catches, but he was averaging 77 receiving yards per game prior to Sunday's 15-yard performance. He will celebrate his 37th birthday Monday and will have a chance to rest up during a Week 5 bye before the Chiefs return to action in Week 6 against the Chargers.

4432708_Marvin Harrison Jr._ARI.headline: Harrison caught one of four targets for 12 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants.
4432708_Marvin Harrison Jr._ARI.story: The struggling third-year WR hit paydirt for the first time this season, connecting with Jacoby Brissett for his only catch of the afternoon in the first quarter to cap the Cardinals' opening drive. Harrison has only five receptions through four games for just 85 yards on a meager 13 targets, and a change of scenery increasingly seems like it might offer his best chance to salvage his career. He'll try to earn a bigger role in the passing game in Week 5 at home against the Lions.

4243331_Cade Otton_TB.headline: Otton caught four of six targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 17-14 loss to the Packers.
4243331_Cade Otton_TB.story: With rookie QB Jalon Daniels making his first career start, he leaned on Otton in the passing game, and the tight end ended up leading the team in receiving yards despite seeing one fewer target than Chris Godwin. Otton has turned 23 targets into 15 catches for 157 yards through four games this season.

3929645_Juwan Johnson_NO.headline: Johnson secured six of eight targets for 59 yards in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
3929645_Juwan Johnson_NO.story: Johnson tied for second in receptions and also finished as the runner-up in receiving yards on the night for the Saints in the lopsided loss. The veteran tight end has gotten the season off to a productive start, recording at least 53 receiving yards in each contest and posting 14 of his 21 catches of the season in the last two games alone. Johnson also has drawn at least seven targets in three of the first four games, affording him a very appealing fantasy floor going into a Week 5 home matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

4429025_Quentin Johnston_LAC.headline: Johnston (chest) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
4429025_Quentin Johnston_LAC.story: A chest injury has resulted in back-to-back capped sessions for Johnston to kick off Week 5 prep, giving him just one more opportunity to get back to full Friday before the Chargers potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's game against the Broncos. With Ladd McConkey (foot) not practicing Wednesday or Thursday and potentially trending toward an absence, an active Johnston likely will be the top pass catcher available to QB Justin Herbert this weekend.

4429205_Jordan Addison_MIN.headline: Addison (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
4429205_Jordan Addison_MIN.story: One day removed from missing Wednesday's practice due to a sore hamstring, Addison rejoined his teammates and fellow WR Justin Jefferson, who missed a Week 4 win against the Dolphins due to an ankle injury but so far has been limited this week. Friday's practice report may provide insight regarding the statuses of both players ahead of Sunday's game at New Orleans.

4242355_Jake Ferguson_DAL.headline: Ferguson caught three of four targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 34-30 win over the Texans.
4242355_Jake Ferguson_DAL.story: Ferguson is averaging a career-low 2.5 yards after catch per reception and just 0.71 yards per route run through four games to begin the season. He has three touchdowns on the year but otherwise has caught just 12 passes for 83 yards on 15 targets in Dallas' high-volume passing attack. He's merely fighting for scraps behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and has devolved into a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

4428850_Dontayvion Wicks_PHI.headline: Wicks was limited at Thursday's practice due to a hamstring injury, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
4428850_Dontayvion Wicks_PHI.story: Wicks' addition to the injury report midweek indicates that he may have picked up the health concern at practice, but he joins DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) as banged-up players at the position. Currently, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey are the Eagles' healthy wide receivers.

4612826_Ladd McConkey_LAC.headline: McConkey (foot) didn't practice Thursday.
4612826_Ladd McConkey_LAC.story: McConkey dealt with a foot injury last week before attempting to play through it this past Sunday in Seattle. He eventually exited for good in the third quarter and hasn't practiced since then. Coach Jim Harbaugh termed McConkey "week-to-week" Monday, according to Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com, so it won't be a surprise if he's ruled out on the Chargers' final Week 5 injury report Friday.

5083076_Harold Fannin Jr._CLE.headline: Fannin secured three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
5083076_Harold Fannin Jr._CLE.story: After surging over the last pair of contests, Fannin had a quiet night somewhat reminiscent of his Week 1 performance against the Jaguars. However, the second-year tight end still rewarded fantasy managers by crossing the goal line for the third time in the last two games on a two-yard catch late in the first half. Fannin does have at least five targets in three straight games, and he should have a good chance of continuing to serve as a key target for a resurgent Deshaun Watson in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

4372016_Jaylen Waddle_DEN.headline: Waddle brought in eight of 10 targets for 138 yards in the Broncos' 20-13 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
4372016_Jaylen Waddle_DEN.story: After a completely non-descript Broncos debut in Week 1, Waddle bounced back with a signature performance in Denver's come-from-behind victory. The veteran wideout led his team in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets by a wide margin, and the highlight of his afternoon was a spectacular 49-yard contested catch early in the second quarter that took the ball down to the Jaguars' one-yard line. The caliber of performance was emblematic of why the Broncos traded for Waddle this offseason, and it may serve as a launchpad for his role in the offense moving forward.

16800_Davante Adams_LA.headline: Adams caught four of nine targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles.
16800_Davante Adams_LA.story: Adams took a back seat to Puka Nacua (hip), who caught nine of 12 targets for 125 yards and scored a two-yard rushing touchdown in the latter's return from a two-game absence. In two games alongside Nacua, Adams has just 58 receiving yards, compared to 332 yards and two touchdowns across the two games Nacua missed. With Nacua available, Adams is likely to play second fiddle again in Week 5 against the Bills.

4360078_Alec Pierce_IND.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen reiterated Monday that Pierce didn't undergo surgery on his left heel and is continuing to rehab the injury, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
4360078_Alec Pierce_IND.story: Ian Rapoport of NFL Network had previously relayed last week that Pierce would avoid another procedure after aggravating his surgically repaired heel in a Sept. 20 loss to the Chiefs, but that report was called into question after the wideout was spotted Sunday moving around the Colts locker room with the aid of a scooter while he had a cast on his left foot. Apparently, Pierce is using the cast for extra protection and using the scooter to keep weight off the injured foot, which he hopes will accelerate the healing process. Pierce is without a timeline to return to game action, but he'll have to miss at least three more contests after landing on injured reserve over the weekend.

4362238_Chase Brown_CIN.headline: Brown rushed nine times for 10 yards and brought in all 11 targets for 71 yards in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
4362238_Chase Brown_CIN.story: Brown had drastically different degrees of success in his two roles, gaining next to nothing on the ground while setting a new career high in receptions. The versatile back's boost in involvement as a pass catcher was at least partly a byproduct of Ja'Marr Chase's first-half exit due to a concussion, and Brown caught Joe Burrow's final pass of the day and was tripped up just a yard short of a first down with 56 seconds remaining to snuff out Cincinnati's final chance at a comeback victory. Brown is averaging just 3.6 yards per carry but has a 21-103-0 receiving line on 24 targets through four games heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

4570037_Terrance Ferguson_LA.headline: Ferguson (soreness) was not listed on the injury report the Rams released Tuesday, according to Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com.
4570037_Terrance Ferguson_LA.story: Ferguson carried an injury designation for the past couple weeks due to an undisclosed injury, but his omission from Tuesday's report indicates it's no longer a concern. Ferguson has been generating some buzz in fantasy circles, but all five of the tight ends on the Rams' depth chart head into Week 1 healthy, so it's unclear exactly what sort of target volume he might see.

3930086_Dawson Knox_BUF.headline: Knox was among the Bills who didn't see action in Saturday's preseason game against the Browns.
3930086_Dawson Knox_BUF.story: The Bills rested most of their key skill players in the contest, a trend that could continue in Thursday's preseason finale against the Steelers. Looking ahead, Knox -- who agreed to a new three-year deal with the team in March -- is once again set to work in tandem with fellow TE Dalton Kincaid, an arrangement that resulted in Knox posting a 36/417/4 receiving line on 49 targets in 17 regular-season games in 2025, while Kincaid turned in a 39/571/5 line in 12 regular-season contests. From a fantasy perspective, Kincaid brings more pass-catching upside to the table, but Knox should still earn enough targets in 2026 to merit roster consideration in deeper formats.

4569173_Rhamondre Stevenson_NE.headline: Stevenson (knee) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
4569173_Rhamondre Stevenson_NE.story: A limited participant in both of the Patriots' first two Week 5 practices, Stevenson still appears to be managing the knee issue he sustained late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over the Bills. The fact that he hasn't been held out of practice entirely is a strong sign that Stevenson will be available for this Sunday's matchup with the Raiders, though he might need to upgrade to full participation Friday to head into the weekend without an injury designation.

3116365_Mark Andrews_BAL.headline: Andrews caught six of seven targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
3116365_Mark Andrews_BAL.story: With Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) out for this one, Andrews finished second on the team in targets, two behind Rashod Bateman, who posted 7-88-1 receiving on his nine looks. Andrews ran 28 routes on Lamar Jackson's 38 dropbacks and is seeing a bigger piece of the pie at tight end this season with Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar now off the team. Through two games, Andrews has 10 catches for 98 yards on 13 targets. He'll be a TE1 next Sunday against the Cowboys in Brazil.

3046439_Hunter Henry_NE.headline: Henry finished with five receptions for 62 yards on five targets in Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills.
3046439_Hunter Henry_NE.story: The catch and yardage totals were season-best marks for Henry, who took the field for 49 of the Patriots' 76 offensive snaps (64.5 percent). With fellow tight end Eli Raridon (ankle) making an early exit from the contest and potentially at risk of missing the Patriots' Week 5 game against the Raiders, Henry could be called upon to handle a heftier workload next Sunday.

3045523_Kendrick Bourne_ARI.headline: Bourne wasn't targeted in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants.
3045523_Kendrick Bourne_ARI.story: Bourne played 42 of 66 offensive snaps and ran 31 routes on Jacoby Brissett's 39 dropbacks, but he's deep down the pecking order for targets behind Trey McBride, Michael Wilson and even Marvin Harrison most of the time. Bourne has 12 grabs for 108 yards on 14 targets through four games.

4248528_Christian Watson_GB.headline: Watson secured all three targets for 47 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
4248528_Christian Watson_GB.story: Watson led the Packers in receiving yards on an afternoon when Jordan Love threw for only 197 yards. The speedy wideout's reception, receiving yardage and target totals were all season lows, but Watson has still enjoyed a productive start to the campaign with a 20-331-4 line on 32 targets and good health throughout. Watson and the Packers' air attack as a whole will look for a boost in production at the expense of the division-rival Bears in a Week 5 home matchup next Sunday.

4362249_Jayden Reed_GB.headline: The Packers officially placed Reed (neck) on injured reserve Wednesday.
4362249_Jayden Reed_GB.story: Coach Matt LaFleur announced earlier Wednesday that Reed required surgery on his neck injury that'll be season-ending, so this transaction was inevitable. Reed has been contained to just nine regular-season appearances the last two years due to health concerns, but LaFleur did relay to Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that he doesn't believe the current issue will threaten the wide receiver's career. With Reed sidelined for the rest of the campaign, Skyy Moore will operate as Green Bay's No. 3 WR behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

4701936_Matthew Golden_GB.headline: Golden brought in three of seven targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also rushed once for six yards.
4701936_Matthew Golden_GB.story: Jordan Love threw for a modest 197 yards overall on the afternoon, so Golden's subdued production can be viewed within that context. The second-year speedster tied with Tucker Kraft for the team lead in targets on the afternoon, and although Golden brought in less than half of them. he recorded his second touchdown grab of the campaign on a two-yard reception early in the second quarter. Golden's reception and yardage totals were season lows, but he's still on pace for a breakout second campaign with an 18-274-2 line going into a Week 5 home divisional matchup against the Bears next Sunday.

4572680_Tucker Kraft_GB.headline: Kraft brought in six of seven targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also rushed once for three yards.
4572680_Tucker Kraft_GB.story: Kraft set the pace for the Packers in receptions and tied with Matthew Golden for the team lead in targets on the afternoon while also finishing as the runner-up in receiving yards for Green Bay. The talented tight end also notched his first touchdown of the season with a two-yard catch early in the second half that was originally ruled out of bounds before being overturned on replay. Kraft has made a remarkable recovery from last year's season-ending knee injury, producing a 15-148-1 line over his first four games heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Bears next Sunday.

3149687_Chris Brooks_GB.headline: Brooks (ankle) didn't practice Thursday.
3149687_Chris Brooks_GB.story: Brooks was held out of practice for a second straight day, and his consecutive absences could put his availability in jeopardy for Sunday's game against the Bears. Perhaps out of concern for Brooks' status heading into the weekend, the Packers signed Pierre Strong off their practice squad Thursday to give the team another healthy option in the backfield behind MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. If Brooks ends up sitting out Sunday, Strong could end up handling some of Brooks' responsibilities on passing downs.

4688813_Josh Downs_IND.headline: Downs caught three of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders.
4688813_Josh Downs_IND.story: Even with Alec Pierce (heel) and Keenan Allen (groin) on the shelf, Downs wound up getting a season low in targets as Indianapolis didn't need to pass the ball much against a Washington team that lost Marcus Mariota (knee) in the first quarter, putting seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis under center. Through four games, Downs is still looking for his first trip to the end zone, posting a 17-202-0 line on 28 targets. He figures to be busier in Week 5 on the road in Pittsburgh.

15818_Keenan Allen_IND.headline: Allen (groin) was limited in practice Thursday.
15818_Keenan Allen_IND.story: It was another limited session for Allen, who is working his way back from a groin injury that kept him out against the Commanders in Week 4. Allen is trending toward being ready to go against the Steelers on Sunday, which would give this receiving corps a much-needed boost.

4431459_Tyler Warren_IND.headline: Warren caught all five of his targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders.
4431459_Tyler Warren_IND.story: The Colts didn't need to air it out much after the Commanders lost Marcus Mariota to a knee injury, putting their offense in the hands of seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, and Warren tied his season low in targets as a result. The tight end still tied Laquon Treadwell for the team high in catches, however. Warren has produced a 23-130-2 line on 27 targets through four games, and he'll remain one of Daniel Jones' top options as long as wideouts Alec Pierce (heel), and Keenan Allen (groin) remain on the shelf.

4686468_Seth McGowan_IND.headline: McGowan turned six carries into 31 yards and caught one of two targets for seven yards during Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders in London. He also returned four kickoffs for 102 yards.
4686468_Seth McGowan_IND.story: McGowan actually saw most of his offensive output in the second quarter with four carries for 18 yards and his seven-yard catch. Most of his on-field production figures to come on special teams as a returner, but the rookie seventh-rounder would be poised for RB1 duties if Jonathan Taylor misses time. The Colts will hit the road for Week 5 against the Steelers this Sunday.

4426388_Jameson Williams_DET.headline: Williams secured six of eight targets for 102 yards in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
4426388_Jameson Williams_DET.story: Williams led the Lions in receiving yards on the night, and all three components of the fourth-year speedster's receiving line were also season-high figures. The productive performance was an especially welcome sight for fantasy managers who were banking on a true breakout season for Williams after back-to-back 1,000-yard campaigns, and the 2022 first-round pick should have a good opportunity to carry over the momentum into a favorable Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

5123663_Isaac TeSlaa_DET.headline: TeSlaa caught all three of his targets for 66 yards in the Lions' 31-24 win over the Jets on Sunday.
5123663_Isaac TeSlaa_DET.story: Detroit's third receiver, TeSlaa played 48 percent of the offensive snaps against New York but made the most of his opportunities and ended up leading the team in receiving yards. With Jameson Williams continuing to struggle to get going early in the season, TeSlaa could start earning a couple more looks from Jared Goff. It's still unlikely to be enough to put TeSlaa in the redraft fantasy mix unless one of Williams or Amon-Ra St. Brown misses time with an injury.

4912274_Sione Vaki_DET.headline: Vaki recorded one carry for seven yards and caught his only target for 13 yards during Thursday's 41-31 loss at Buffalo.
4912274_Sione Vaki_DET.story: Vaki was on the field for 11 of the Lions' 65 offensive snaps in Week 2, a similar workload to what he saw in Week 1. Barring an injury to starter Jahmyr Gibbs, Vaki seems unlikely to get the ball more than a couple times in any given game.

4258173_Nico Collins_HOU.headline: Collins caught seven of eight targets for 118 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
4258173_Nico Collins_HOU.story: Making his return from a two-game absence due to a hamstring strain, Collins led the Texans in catches, targets and scrimmage yards while hauling in C.J. Stroud's only two TD passes of the day. While Houston is a disastrous 0-4 to start the season, the offense has scored 61 points in the two games Collins has been active for and just 23 in the two games he missed. The star wideout will look to come up big again in Week 5 on the road in Tennessee.

4586312_Jaylin Noel_HOU.headline: Noel caught all three targets for 85 yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys. He added four rushing yards on one attempt.
4586312_Jaylin Noel_HOU.story: Despite Nico Collins (hamstring) returning to the lineup after missing two games, Noel remained a big part of the offense, as Xavier Hutchinson was the big loser in terms of snaps and routes. Noel ran just one fewer route than Kayshon Boutte and six fewer than Collins. Through four games, Noel has nine catches for 186 yards on 12 targets. He has a chance to become the Texans' WR2 behind Collins at some point this season, especially if Boutte doesn't start producing.

3117256_Dalton Schultz_HOU.headline: Schultz caught both of his targets for nine yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
3117256_Dalton Schultz_HOU.story: With Nico Collins back from his hamstring injury after missing two weeks, Schultz's voluminous pass-catching role evaporated against Dallas. For as long as Collins is healthy, Schultz is little more than a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option ahead of next Sunday's date with the Titans.

4432577_C.J. Stroud_HOU.headline: Stroud completed 21 of 31 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys. He added 12 yards on two carries.
4432577_C.J. Stroud_HOU.story: With top receiver Nico Collins back in the fold after a hamstring strain, Stroud posted his best numbers of the season -- he threw for 353 yards in Week 2, but it came on 55 attempts and he didn't produce a TD. Both of Stroud's scores Sunday went to Collins, and through four games he has a 5:0 TD:INT, with his only two turnovers being a pair of Week 1 fumbles. The fourth-year QB will try to lead Houston to its first win of the year in a Week 5 road trip to Tennessee.

4429059_Woody Marks_HOU.headline: Marks rushed six times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to reel in his only target during Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
4429059_Woody Marks_HOU.story: Marks logged four fewer carries than David Montgomery (10), but he was able to notch a six-yard score in the fourth quarter. The running back now has reached the end zone in back-to-back contests as he attempts to eat into Montgomery's workload in the backfield. Neither running back is a particularly appealing option in fantasy at the moment, but Marks is trending in the right direction.

4047650_DK Metcalf_PIT.headline: Metcalf brought in five of nine targets for 115 yards in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
4047650_DK Metcalf_PIT.story: Metcalf led the Steelers across the stat sheet in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his production in the first two categories also qualified as new season highs. The veteran wideout started slowly, but he came on with catches of 43, 22 and 28 yards in the fourth quarter. The standout night was a welcome sight for fantasy managers, who'd seen Metcalf post an inefficient and modest 11-98-1 line on 24 targets over his first three games. Metcalf will aim to carry over the momentum into a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

4035687_Michael Pittman Jr._PIT.headline: Pittman is expected to miss multiple weeks after aggravating his foot injury, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports Thursday.
4035687_Michael Pittman Jr._PIT.story: Pittman missed Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots due to a foot injury and had just four catches for 31 yards across two subsequent appearances. He's facing a multi-week absence after aggravating that injury in practice leading up to the Steelers' Week 5 matchup against the Colts. The team has yet to decide whether to place Pittman on IR, in which case he would be required to sit out a minimum of four weeks.

4431492_Roman Wilson_PIT.headline: Wilson brought in three of six targets for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
4431492_Roman Wilson_PIT.story: Wilson capped off a marathon 17-play opening drive for the Steelers by showcasing his speed, as the second-year wideout scored from 12 yards out on a shovel pass from Aaron Rodgers. Wilson has at least three catches in each of his first four games, and Thursday's yardage total established a new season high after he'd also done so with his 60-yard tally in Week 3. Wilson also has exactly six targets in each contest thus far, cementing him as a key complementary component of the air attack heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

4361411_Pat Freiermuth_PIT.headline: Freiermuth brought in three of five targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
4361411_Pat Freiermuth_PIT.story: Freiermuth and fellow tight end Darnell Washington each had three catches and a touchdown on five targets, as the two continued in a pretty even timeshare at the position. Freiermuth's scoring grab was particularly timely, as it came with 1:42 remaining and put the Steelers within two points of knotting the game up at 24-24. Freiermuth has multiple receptions in every game this season and a pair of touchdown catches, and he should remain in a similar role when Pittsburgh returns to action in a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

4432773_Brian Thomas Jr._JAX.headline: Thomas secured both targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
4432773_Brian Thomas Jr._JAX.story: Thomas was a minimal part of the air attack once again, but that description also applied to fellow wideouts Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington as the Bengals did an effective job taking away Trevor Lawrence's primary targets. However, Thomas was able to break through with what turned out to be a key score, as he recorded a seven-yard scoring grab late in the first half in a game that was ultimately decided by five points. Thomas  still has a modest nine receptions for 105 yards and Sunday's touchdown on 15 targets as the Jaguars head across the pond to face the Eagles in London in Week 5.

3916433_Jakobi Meyers_JAX.headline: Meyers caught three of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 22-17 win against the Bengals.
3916433_Jakobi Meyers_JAX.story: Meyers finished second on the team in targets behind tight end Brenton Strange (eight), but his performance was far from noteworthy. The wide receiver has operated as a distant No. 2 option behind Parker Washington at his position this season, and Sunday's performance was his third game with 40 or fewer receiving yards over four contests.

4430539_Brenton Strange_JAX.headline: Strange caught seven of eight targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Bengals.
4430539_Brenton Strange_JAX.story: Cincinnati annually plays bad defense against opposing tight ends, and Strange was able to take advantage of the clean matchup by leading the team in targets, catches and receiving yards Sunday. An every-down tight end in Jacksonville's potent offense, he's a weekly fringe TE1/2 headed into next Sunday's game against the Eagles. On the season, Strange has 14 catches for 167 yards and one touchdown on 18 targets.

4362619_Chris Rodriguez Jr._JAX.headline: Rodriguez rushed six times for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Bengals.
4362619_Chris Rodriguez Jr._JAX.story: After a slow start to the season, Rodriguez has found the end zone in back-to-back games, this time scoring from 25 yards out for his longest run of the season. Rodriguez has handled exactly six carries in three of the four games and remains a total zero in the passing game with zero targets. He's the definition of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet playing behind Bhayshul Tuten.

4430878_Jaxon Smith-Njigba_SEA.headline: Smith-Njigba gathered in five of six targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 30-23 win against the Chargers.
4430878_Jaxon Smith-Njigba_SEA.story: Smith-Njigba's 27-405-6 line on 36 targets through three games to kick off the campaign perhaps wasn't sustainable, but his Week 4 performance was nothing to sniff at considering he paced the Seahawks in targets among QB Sam Darnold's 22 pass attempts. Smith-Njigba put up at least as many receiving yards in 15 of his 17 regular-season appearances in 2025 as he did Sunday, so a bounce-back seems likely when he takes the field next Sunday versus the 49ers.

4032473_Rashid Shaheed_SEA.headline: Shaheed caught one of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers. He added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown.
4032473_Rashid Shaheed_SEA.story: Shaheed had been mostly nonexistent through the first three games of the season, totaling 57 yards on seven touches, but he was able to break out for a long touchdown in this one, scoring from 28 yards out as a rusher in the second quarter. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba completely dominating the targets in Seattle's passing game, Shaheed has remained a low-floor fantasy option early on in 2026.

2977187_Cooper Kupp_SEA.headline: Kupp caught one of two targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
2977187_Cooper Kupp_SEA.story: Kupp played 34 of 60 offensive snaps and ran 17 routes on Sam Darnold's 26 dropbacks. The veteran wide receiver has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of the first four games, totaling nine grabs for 114 yards and a touchdown on 12 targets. He's well off the fantasy radar with Jaxon Smith-Njigba dominating the looks in Seattle.

4429835_George Holani_SEA.headline: Holani (ribs) remained limited in Thursday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
4429835_George Holani_SEA.story: Holani played through the issue last Sunday against the Chargers and turned eight touches into 20 yards as the change-of-pace back behind Emanuel Wilson. He should fill a similar role again this Sunday against the 49ers. Holani has minimal fantasy appeal.

4597500_Adonai Mitchell_NYJ.headline: Mitchell (finger) wasn't present for warmups at the start of Thursday's practice, Al Iannazzone of Newsday reports.
4597500_Adonai Mitchell_NYJ.story: Mitchell is headed for a second consecutive practice absence ahead of Sunday's home game against the Browns. Head coach Aaron Glenn recently described Mitchell, who missed the past two games, as week-to-week.

4723820_Omar Cooper Jr._NYJ.headline: The Jets placed Cooper (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
4723820_Omar Cooper Jr._NYJ.story: Cooper thus will miss at least the next four games after he suffered a sprained ankle in his pro debut this past Sunday in Tennessee. His next chance for game action will be a Week 6 road matchup with the Patriots on Sunday, Oct. 18, and in the meantime, the Jets will operate with a receiving corps composed of Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Isaiah Williams and Arian Smith.

4685247_Braelon Allen_NYJ.headline: Allen rushed 14 times for 59 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
4685247_Braelon Allen_NYJ.story: Allen accounted for all 14 of the Jets' rushing attempts in the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps), who is considered week-to-week. The Bears dominated time of possession as Geno Smith completed just eight passes in the loss. If Hall isn't ready to return in Week 5 against the Browns, Allen would retain the lead role in the backfield for the Jets.

4361370_Chris Olave_NO.headline: Olave (rest/foot) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
4361370_Chris Olave_NO.story: The Saints held a walkthrough Wednesday, during which Olave logged a rest day. As of Thursday, he mixed back into drills, but a foot injury was added to the practice report after his capped session. His ability to handle some reps while dealing with a health concern generally is a good sign that his status isn't in question for Week 5, but Friday's injury report will reveal whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest versus the Vikings.

4569559_Devaughn Vele_NO.headline: Vele secured six of nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
4569559_Devaughn Vele_NO.story: Vele tied for second in receptions and checked in as the runner-up in targets for the Saints on the night, and he rounded out a solid fantasy performance by recording a three-yard touchdown reception with 1:13 remaining. The score was ultimately meaningless to the outcome of the lopsided loss, but Vele further cemented his standing as a relatively high-volume No. 2 receiver by tying his season high in targets. Vele will take a 21-226-2 line on 31 targets into a Week 5 home matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

4879276_Bryce Lance_NO.headline: Lance turned five targets into a seven-yard catch during the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday.
4879276_Bryce Lance_NO.story: Lance finished fifth on the Saints in targets from quarterback Tyler Shough, though each of the four misses between the duo came on deep passes. After catching three of four targets for 42 yards in his NFL debut against the Lions in Week 1, Lance has just two catches (on nine targets) for 15 yards over his last three games. He'll continue to operate as the Saints' WR3 behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. Lance's playing time likely will take a significant hit once fellow rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is cleared to return from injured reserve, though ESPN's Adam Schefter notes that Week 7 against the Steelers is the earliest targeted return for Tyson. The Saints will stay at home for Week 5 against the Vikings and their aggressive defense.

3054850_Alvin Kamara_NO.headline: Kamara (back) practiced in a limited fashion Thursday.
3054850_Alvin Kamara_NO.story: Kamara was held out of Wednesday's walkthrough due to a back injury, but his upgrade in activity one day later is a decent sign that he's trending in the right direction for Sunday's game against the Vikings. Friday's practice report will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation.

4241389_CeeDee Lamb_DAL.headline: Lamb caught 17 of 21 targets for 189 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-30 win over the Texans.
4241389_CeeDee Lamb_DAL.story: Per RJ Ochoa of Blogging The Boys, it was just the fourth time in NFL history, and the first since Brandon  Marshall in 2009, that a player recorded 17-plus receptions, 180-plus yards and a TD in a single game. Lamb's final catch was his biggest, as he connected with Dak Prescott for a 12-yard score with just 40 seconds left on the clock to complete a comeback from a 10-point halftime deficit. The 17 catches and 21 targets were career highs for the five-time Pro Bowler, and the yardage total was his best since Week 17 of 2023, when Lamb erupted for 227 yards against the Lions. Lamb will take a massive 37-498-4 line on 46 targets through four games, and a three-game streak of 100-plus receiving yards, into a Week 5 home tilt against the Buccaneers.

4426354_George Pickens_DAL.headline: Pickens caught two of three targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 34-30 win over the Texans.
4426354_George Pickens_DAL.story: CeeDee Lamb was the target on a massive 21 of Dak Prescott's 45 pass attempts, which didn't leave much volume for any other Cowboy. Pickens made an impact when he got a chance however, hauling in receptions of 53 and 22 yards. Pickens is still looking for his first TD of 2026 after scoring a career-high nine last season, and he'll take an 18-225-0 line on 28 targets through four games into a Week 5 meeting at home against the Buccaneers.

5083754_Ryan Flournoy_DAL.headline: Flournoy caught four of five targets for 37 yards in Dallas' 34-30 win over the Texans on Sunday.
5083754_Ryan Flournoy_DAL.story: His five targets were actually tied for second on the team, but it was a distant second behind CeeDee Lamb's 21 on Dak Prescott's 45 attempts. Flournoy continues to run plenty of routes as Dallas' top slot receiver between Lamb and George Pickens, but with that duo accounting for most of the receiving production in any given week, Flournoy likely will need an absence from one of them to become usable in fantasy.

4240603_Malik Davis_DAL.headline: The Cowboys placed Davis (hip) on injured reserve Saturday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
4240603_Malik Davis_DAL.story: Davis underwent surgery Saturday for a hip injury, and Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports that the procedure will sideline the 27-year-old running back for the entire 2026 season. With Davis on the shelf, the Cowboys bolstered their backfield depth by signing Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster, with the latter serving as the RB3 behind Javonte Williams and Emari Demercado.

4047646_A.J. Brown_NE.headline: Brown (ankle) was seen in the locker room Wednesday without a noticeable limp, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
4047646_A.J. Brown_NE.story: When Brown came out of Week 1 with a right high-ankle sprain, he was expected to be sidelined for up to six weeks, but his placement on IR before Week 2 action means he's eligible to return to practice as soon as next week. That doesn't mean he actually will be, but being able to move about sans limp generally is a good sign in his recovery and could mean practice reps are on the horizon for the Patriots' No. 1 wide receiver.

4432710_TreVeyon Henderson_NE.headline: Henderson rushed 14 times for 42 yards and failed to bring in either of his two targets in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday.
4432710_TreVeyon Henderson_NE.story: Henderson struggled to get anything going against an improved Bills run defense, averaging an even 3.0 yards per carry. The second-year pro logged one more carry than backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson but finished with five fewer rushing yards, and through three games, Henderson is averaging a pedestrian 3.7 yards per tote while only adding one catch for six yards. The 2025 second-round pick's next opportunity for his first breakout effort of 2026 comes in a Week 5 home matchup against a vastly improved Raiders team.

4040655_Darnell Mooney_NYG.headline: Mooney caught two passes on three targets for 20 yards and logged a nine-yard carry during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
4040655_Darnell Mooney_NYG.story: Mooney has logged two catches in each of the first three games of the season, and his 95 receiving yards are third-most on the Giants behind tight end Isaiah Likely (124) and Malik Nabers (96). The Giants will stay home in Week 4 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up the second-most fantasy points to wide receivers this season.

4682648_Malachi Fields_NYG.headline: Fields caught two of three targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Cardinals.
4682648_Malachi Fields_NYG.story: Fields has emerged as the Giants' clear WR3 in terms of routes, as he ran 22 routes to Malik Nabers' 30 and Darnell Mooney's 26 against Arizona. On the season, Fields has out-targeted Mooney 15 to 10. Fields caught a 12-yard score from Jameis Winston on Sunday, and now has eight catches for 126 yards and the one score through four contests to begin his rookie season.

4361050_Isaiah Likely_NYG.headline: Likely (knee/groin) practiced on a limited basis Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
4361050_Isaiah Likely_NYG.story: Likely maintained his activity level from Wednesday's session as he deals with knee and groin injuries. There's been nothing to suggest that he's in danger of missing Sunday's game at Washington, but he still may be tagged with a designation on the Giants' final practice report of the week Friday.

4689114_Jaxson Dart_NYG.headline: Dart recently underwent surgery to repair the meniscus and MCL in his left knee, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
4689114_Jaxson Dart_NYG.story: Dart's ACL and PCL were apparently spared, but the quarterback remains done for the 2026 regular season after he was injured in the first quarter of Week 2 against the Rams. It's unclear if Dart could make a postseason return if the Giants are able to make it that far. Jameis Winston and newly acquired J.J. McCarthy will handle quarterback duties moving forward this season.

4360516_Tyrone Tracy Jr._NYG.headline: Tracy (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
4360516_Tyrone Tracy Jr._NYG.story: Tracy upgraded his practice participation level in each of the Giants' Week 4 prep sessions. The running back went from a DNP on Wednesday to limited Thursday before finally achieving full participation Friday, in time to avoid an injury designation. Tracy is set to suit up for Sunday's game as the No. 3 option behind Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris.

4241463_Jerry Jeudy_CLE.headline: Jeudy caught all three of his targets for 36 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over Pittsburgh.
4241463_Jerry Jeudy_CLE.story: It looked like Jeudy could be shut out for the third straight game after finishing the first half with no targets. However, the veteran wideout gave Cleveland a first down with a nine-yard reception late in the third quarter, then came up with two big catches -- a 17-yarder and a 10-yarder -- after the two-minute warning in the fourth to help set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. The two fourth-quarter catches alone accounted for more yardage than Jeudy had recorded across his first three games of the campaign, so perhaps he and QB Deshaun Watson have found some chemistry that they can carry over into a Week 5 matchup versus the Jets.

4870653_KC Concepcion_CLE.headline: Concepcion secured five of eight targets for 64 yards and returned two punts for 10 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
4870653_KC Concepcion_CLE.story: Concepcion and fellow rookie Denzel Boston continued to spark the Browns' air attack Thursday, and the former finished second in receptions and receiving yards while setting the pace in targets. Concepcion's catch and yardage totals also qualified as new career highs, and the productive night served as a welcome bounce-back effort after the rookie first-round pick had been held to 2-9-0 receiving line in the Week 3 win over the Panthers. He should continue to garner plenty of Deshaun Watson's attention in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

4832800_Denzel Boston_CLE.headline: Boston brought in four of seven targets for 89 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
4832800_Denzel Boston_CLE.story: The impressive start to Boston's NFL career continued Thursday, with the rookie second-round pick leading the Browns in receiving yards and tying for runner-up status with Quinshon Judkins in targets. The bulk of Boston's production came on an impressive 60-yard reception to kick off an early second-quarter possession that culminated in a Judkins two-yard touchdown run. Boston has quickly amassed a 13-284-2 line on 22 targets through his first four career games, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

3122840_Deshaun Watson_CLE.headline: Watson completed 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards with one touchdown and one interception while rushing seven times for 22 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday. He also committed two fumbles, losing one.
3122840_Deshaun Watson_CLE.story: Watson's rather unlikely comeback season continued in the primetime spotlight Thursday against a division rival, with the embattled veteran ultimately besting future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers. Watson's late third-quarter fumble on a sack by T.J. Watt didn't result in any Steelers points, but his interception on Cleveland's ensuing possession on a deep pass intended for Denzel Boston did lead to Pittsburgh's penultimate touchdown of the night. Watson was otherwise impressive, recording his highest passing yardage total since Week 3 of the 2023 season. Watson connected with seven different targets overall, and his one scoring strike went to Harold Fannin from two yards out late in the second quarter. Watson now boasts a 69.6 percent completion rate -- his highest since the 2020 season in Houston -- and a 6:2 TD:INT alongside 127 rushing yards heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

5081397_Dylan Sampson_CLE.headline: Sampson (knee) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
5081397_Dylan Sampson_CLE.story: It's unclear exactly how much time Sampson will miss. He is expected back this season, per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer, but his placement on IR means he will miss at least the next four games. Jaleel McLaughlin was brought up from the practice squad, and both he and Raheim Sanders -- who played 18 snaps on offense and got four touches Sunday after Sampson's exit -- will work behind starter Quinshon Judkins.

4686612_Tre' Harris_LAC.headline: Harris caught three of five targets for 60 yards during Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks.
4686612_Tre' Harris_LAC.story: Harris led the team in receiving yards for the second straight week, recording at least 53 receiving yards for the third contest in a row. Ladd McConkey (foot) aggravated his pre-existing foot injury in the contest, and he is considered week-to-week for the time being. If McConkey is unavailable in Week 5 versus the Broncos, Harris may have a chance to operate as the team's primary pass catcher.

4241263_Charlie Kolar_LAC.headline: Kolar (forearm) remained limited in Thursday's practice.
4241263_Charlie Kolar_LAC.story: Kolar broke his forearm in Week 2 against the Raiders and has missed the last two games.
