The block-first tight end's return will be welcomed by Los Angeles once he's cleared. The Chargers' offensive line has been a nightmare, and both starting tackles Rashawn Slater (ankle) and Joe Alt (neck) are again dealing with injuries.

4596334_Keaton Mitchell_LAC.headline: Mitchell tallied 10 carries for 39 yards and five catches (on six targets) for 24 yards during Sunday's 30-23 defeat at Seattle.
4596334_Keaton Mitchell_LAC.story: Mitchell surprisingly led the Chargers backfield in touches with 15, ahead of Omarion Hampton's 11 and Kimani Vidal's seven, but unlike his position mates he didn't reach the end zone. Because Mitchell's touch count has increased in each successive week this season, he's trending in a positive direction, but until one of the trio is handling most of the RB reps, it'll be difficult to trust any of them for fantasy purposes on a weekly basis. He next takes the field next Sunday against the Broncos.

3915416_DJ Moore_BUF.headline: Moore (shoulder) was not participating during the media viewing period of Thursday's practice,  Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
3915416_DJ Moore_BUF.story: Moore has not been ruled out for the Week 5 matchup against the Rams, but it seems he's got an uphill battle ahead of him. He aggravated his shoulder injury in the Week 4 loss to the Patriots and did not return to action. He may get some work in later in Thursday's practice, but the official injury report will tell the tale.

4373678_Khalil Shakir_BUF.headline: Shakir turned seven catches (on eight targets) into 82 yards during the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
4373678_Khalil Shakir_BUF.story: Shakir's final stat line Sunday nearly matched his 8-94-0 line on 15 targets across the first three games of the regular season. Most of the veteran slot receiver's yards came on a 51-yard connection with Josh Allen late in the second quarter, with the latter finishing the drive with a two-yard rushing touchdown. Unfortunately for Shakir, he also had the ball ripped out of his hands by Robert Spillane within the final seconds of the first half, though the Bills avoided any damage after the defense intercepted Patriots quarterback Drake Maye on the very next play. DJ Moore aggravated a previous shoulder injury during Sunday's loss, and while it's not considered a long-term issue, Bills pass catchers like Shakir, Keon Coleman and tight end Dalton Kincaid are all candidates to see more targets from Allen if Moore cannot play in Week 5 against the Rams on Monday, Oct. 12.

4635008_Keon Coleman_BUF.headline: Coleman secured six of seven targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
4635008_Keon Coleman_BUF.story: DJ Moore went down in the first half with a shoulder injury, opening up plenty of opportunity in the Bills' air attack. Coleman almost fully maximized his additional targets, recording a team-high yardage figure while finishing second in both receptions and targets. Coleman's first two pro seasons were marked by inconsistency, but the third-year wideout has secured 14 of 16 targets for 217 yards and a touchdown over the first four games of 2026, and 10 of his catches have resulted in first downs. Coleman's 34-yard touchdown grab Sunday also would have delivered the game-winning points had Drake Maye not mounted a successful drive on the ensuing possession, and Coleman could remain in an elevated role during a Week 5 road matchup against the Rams on Monday night, Oct. 12, if Moore is sidelined for that contest.

4385690_Dalton Kincaid_BUF.headline: Kincaid brought in one of two targets for seven yards in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
4385690_Dalton Kincaid_BUF.story: Kincaid saw a reduced role in the air attack for the second straight week, although Sunday's downturn resulted in season-low figures across the board. Kincaid opened the season with a 12-225-0 line over the first two games, but he's managed just three receptions for 45 yards on five targets in the subsequent pair of contests. Kincaid will look to bounce back in a Week 5 marquee matchup on the road against the Rams on Monday night, Oct. 12.

3918298_Josh Allen_BUF.headline: Allen completed 23 of 33 passes for 253 yards with a touchdown and an interception and added five carries for four yards and another score in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
3918298_Josh Allen_BUF.story: Allen lost No. 1 receiver DJ Moore to a shoulder injury in the first half, but he still put together a serviceable passing line that included a 34-yard touchdown pass to Keon Coleman with just over four minutes remaining that erased a 21-20 deficit. That scoring play was preceded by Allen's two-yard touchdown run late in the first half, already his seventh rushing score of the campaign. However, Allen was also responsible for snuffing out Buffalo's last chance at a comeback after New England had answered his touchdown pass with a score of its own, as he threw an interception on a deep pass intended for Joshua Palmer with 1:14 remaining. The star signal-caller will aim to atone in a tough Week 5 road showdown against the Rams on Monday night, Oct. 12.

4429501_Ray Davis_BUF.headline: Davis logged a four-yard carry, a three-yard reception and returned one kickoff for 29 yards during the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots in Week 4.
4429501_Ray Davis_BUF.story: Both of Davis' offensive outputs came on back-to-back plays early in the second quarter, and his four snaps on offense were well behind starter James Cook (35) and backup Ty Johnson (19). Even as a returner, Davis took a back seat to Greg Dortch, the latter of whom returned four kickoffs for 91 yards and two punts for 16 yards. Davis' production on offense and special teams will continue to be limited unless one of Cook, Johnson or Dortch were to miss time.

4567750_Emeka Egbuka_TB.headline: Egbuka brought in two of four targets for 13 yards in the Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
4567750_Emeka Egbuka_TB.story: Egbuka's production downturn was at least partly the result of Jalon Daniels' up-and-down NFL debut under center. The second-year wideout was third in targets and tied for third in receptions with multiple teammates on the afternoon, but Egbuka's yardage total, which was a season low, bested only that of Kameron Johnson's (three yards) in the loss. Egbuka now has a 15-154-1 line on 24 targets over his first four games, and with Baker Mayfield (thumb) reportedly in line to miss up to a total of seven weeks, the former will have to progressively build chemistry with Daniels to retain solid fantasy value.

3116165_Chris Godwin Jr._TB.headline: Godwin brought in six of seven targets for 31 yards in the Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
3116165_Chris Godwin Jr._TB.story: Godwin led the Buccaneers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards on the afternoon. The latter total was especially nothing to write home about, but it was the byproduct of rookie Jalon Daniels throwing for only 148 yards in his NFL debut. Godwin and the rest of the Buccaneers' air attack currently have fairly dim prospects while Daniels takes his initial lumps at the NFL level, and with Baker Mayfield (thumb) unlikely to return before November per latest reports, the veteran receiver has limited fantasy value for the foreseeable future.

4430834_Jalen McMillan_TB.headline: The Buccaneers placed McMillan (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday.
4430834_Jalen McMillan_TB.story: The move to IR officially rules McMillan out for the Buccaneers' next four games, but the wideout is projected to miss around 6-to-8 weeks after he sustained a PCL sprain of his left knee during Sunday's loss to the Vikings. With McMillan sidelined, rookie third-round pick Ted Hurst should be locked in as the Buccaneers' No. 3 wideout behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin.

3052587_Baker Mayfield_TB.headline: Mayfield's dislocated right thumb could keep him out anywhere from 3-to-6 weeks, depending on how quickly he's able to resume gripping the football without issue, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
3052587_Baker Mayfield_TB.story: Head coach Todd Bowles previously acknowledged that Mayfield would miss at least three weeks due to the injury, which he sustained in last Sunday's loss to the Vikings. Though Mayfield was cleared of any tendon or ligament damage and won't need surgery on the thumb on his throwing hand, the two-time Pro Bowler required stitches to close a wound caused by the dislocation. Despite facing a loose recovery timeline that could keep him out for more than four games, Mayfield avoided placement on injured reserve Saturday, which signals that the Buccaneers are still holding out hope that he might be ready to go after a three-week absence. For however long Mayfield ends up being sidelined, the Buccaeneers will turn to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels to direct the offense, beginning with Sunday's game versus Green Bay.

4371733_Kenny Gainwell_TB.headline: Gainwell rushed three times for five yards in Sunday's 17-14 loss to the Packers. He added two catches for 22 yards and a touchdown on two targets.
4371733_Kenny Gainwell_TB.story: Gainwell was out-snapped 36 to 26 by Bucky Irving, who also handled 16 carries to Gainwell's three in Jalon Daniels' first career start at quarterback. Gainwell was the only running back to see a target out of the backfield for Tampa Bay, and he scored his first touchdown of 2026 with a 10-yard catch in the fourth quarter. Averaging just 5.25 touches per game, Gainwell isn't a recommended fantasy target in a broken Tampa Bay offense.

4871023_Carnell Tate_TEN.headline: Tate (back) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
4871023_Carnell Tate_TEN.story: This is a new injury for Tate, who practiced without limitations Wednesday. The rookie fourth overall pick is coming off the best performance of his young NFL career, as Tate compiled nine catches for 145 yards in this past Sunday's 28-14 loss to the Ravens. A return to full participation Friday would help Tate avoid taking an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Texans.

4569587_Wan'Dale Robinson_TEN.headline: Robinson caught three of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Ravens.
4569587_Wan'Dale Robinson_TEN.story: Robinson was able to find paydirt for the second straight week, connecting with quarterback Cam Ward for a three-yard touchdown with 1:16 left in regulation. The wide receiver finished second on the team in targets behind rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate (12), and Robinson has now caught 16 of 23 targets for 123 yards and two touchdowns over the first four contests of the 2026 campaign.

4686728_Gunnar Helm_TEN.headline: Helm was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice due to a knee injury.
4686728_Gunnar Helm_TEN.story: Helm didn't appear on the Titans' initial Week 5 injury report posted Wednesday, so his limited participation Thursday could be indicate that he hurt his knee at some point during practice. The Titans will see what Helm is able to do during the final practice of the week Friday before determining if he'll take a designation into Sunday's game against the Texans. The tight end has played more than 70 percent of snaps in each of Tennessee's first four contests but has been a minor part of the passing attack, stringing together a 9-60-0 receiving line on 12 targets.

4688380_Cam Ward_TEN.headline: Ward completed 20 of 31 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Ravens. He added 27 yards on four carries and threw a two-point conversion.
4688380_Cam Ward_TEN.story: The Titans were down 24-7 at halftime, but with Lamar Jackson (ankle) forced to the sideline, Ward was nearly able to engineer a comeback. The second-year QB found Wan'Dale Robinson for a three-yard score inside the final two minutes of the fourth quarter, but an onside-kick attempt didn't succeed, and Ward never got the ball back. He still has a modest 3:2 TD:INT through four games, with another two touchdowns on the ground, and his 222 passing yards Sunday were a season high, but Ward might be building some momentum heading into a Week 5 home tilt against the Texans.

4428557_Tyjae Spears_TEN.headline: Spears turned two carries into seven yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-1 yard during the Titans' 24-18 loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
4428557_Tyjae Spears_TEN.story: Spears played a total of 23 offensive snaps, which was behind starter Tony Pollard (34) and ahead of rookie Nicholas Singleton (eight). Still, Spears' three touches were far behind Pollard's 20 (16 carries, four catches), while Singleton ended up with one more carry than Spears. It looks like Spears will have a tough time seeing a sizable and consistent workload in Titans offensive game plans unless Pollard were to miss time, though the veteran running back is a name to watch ahead of the trade deadline due to him being in the final year of his contract, per Adam Schefter of ESPN. Tennessee will face Houston in Week 5, with both teams looking to earn their first win of the 2026 season.

4362628_Ja'Marr Chase_CIN.headline: Chase (concussion) was officially listed as a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
4362628_Ja'Marr Chase_CIN.story: Chase took a step in the right direction Thursday after being unable to practice Wednesday. In order to have a chance to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol in time to suit up Sunday against the Dolphins, Chase would need to practice without limitations Friday. He was diagnosed with a concussion after exiting this past Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in the first half.

4239993_Tee Higgins_CIN.headline: Higgins (groin/neck) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
4239993_Tee Higgins_CIN.story: Higgins was seen working out off to the side during the open portion of Thursday's session, and he apparently wasn't able to mix into team drills once practice was closed to the media. The veteran wideout has now had consecutive absences from practice to kick off Week 5 prep, while No. 1 receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) bumped up to limited participation Thursday after sitting out Wednesday. The Bengals will see if Higgins and Chase can increase their practice activity Friday before deciding if either or both wideouts will carry designations into Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

4368003_Andrei Iosivas_CIN.headline: The Bengals placed Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve Saturday.
4368003_Andrei Iosivas_CIN.story: Iosivas is having surgery to repair a torn ligament in his thumb, necessitating his move to injured reserve. As such, he will not be allowed to play for at least the next four games, so the earliest Iosivas can return is Week 8 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 1. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins will continue to serve as the Bengals' top pass catchers, but in Iosivas' absence, there are more offensive snaps available for rookie fourth-rounder Colbie Young, Dohnte Meyers and Ke'Shawn Williams.

3116164_Mike Gesicki_CIN.headline: Gesicki caught three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars.
3116164_Mike Gesicki_CIN.story: With Ja'Marr Chase leaving early in the first half with a concussion, Gesicki played an elevated role behind Tee Higgins and Chase Brown in the Cincinnati offense. Gesicki continues to run the vast majority of his routes out of the slot and should remain in that role while Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is on injured reserve. Gesicki has scored a touchdown in three of the first four games to begin the season and is up to 11 catches for 155 yards and the three scores on 15 targets.

4429615_Zay Flowers_BAL.headline: The Ravens listed Flowers (hamstring) as a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
4429615_Zay Flowers_BAL.story: As anticipated after he was spotted working out off to the side during the media-access portion of practice, Flowers went down as a non-participant for the second consecutive day. The wideout hasn't practiced in any fashion since tweaking his hamstring in the Ravens' season-opening win over the Colts, and he could be trending toward missing a second straight game this Sunday against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. The Ravens were scheduled to fly to Brazil on Thursday, and, per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, Flowers made the trip, so it seems as if he at least has a chance to play Week 3.

4870847_Ja'Kobi Lane_BAL.headline: Coach Jesse Minter said Lane underwent wrist surgery Wednesday, and the Ravens placed the rookie wide receiver on injured reserve, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
4870847_Ja'Kobi Lane_BAL.story: Lane left the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis with a wrist injury that eventually was confirmed to include a fracture. With his move to IR, he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, meaning his next chance for game action will come Oct. 18 at Cleveland. As long as Lane is sidelined, Zay Flowers (hamstring), Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker (groin), Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester will be among those that could see additional action at wide receiver for Baltimore.

4038441_Justice Hill_BAL.headline: Hill rushed twice for six yards and caught two targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
4038441_Justice Hill_BAL.story: Hill was on the field for 27 of the Ravens' 58 offensive snaps. The running back saw usage as both runner and receiver, providing a fast contrast to Derrick Henry's bulk. It appears Hill may be on track for more consistent complementary opportunities than last season behind Derrick Henry in Baltimore's new offense.

4262921_Justin Jefferson_MIN.headline: Jefferson (ankle) was limited at practice Thursday.
4262921_Justin Jefferson_MIN.story: Jefferson initially injured his ankle in the middle of a Week 3 win at Tampa Bay and missed this past Sunday's game against the Dolphins. So far this week, he's logged back-to-back capped sessions, and Friday's practice report may provide some clarity regarding whether or not a return to action Sunday in New Orleans is possible. For what it's worth, Jefferson told Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com on Wednesday that he wants to play this weekend as a native of Louisiana, but ultimately it'll be a team decision regarding his status.

3886598_Jauan Jennings_MIN.headline: Jennings caught his lone target for eight yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
3886598_Jauan Jennings_MIN.story: Despite Justin Jefferson (ankle) missing Sunday's game, Jennings remained a non-factor on offense, as he took a distant back seat to all three of T.J. Hockenson, Jordan Addison and Aaron Jones. Jennings has two catches for nine yards on four targets across 152 offensive snaps through three games this season. He's well off the fantasy radar.

4036133_T.J. Hockenson_MIN.headline: Hockenson caught all 13 of his targets for 119 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
4036133_T.J. Hockenson_MIN.story: The veteran tight end emerged as Kyler Murray's favorite target in the absence of Justin Jefferson (ankle), and as a result Hockenson produced his first game with 100-plus yards since 2024, when he popped for a 7-114-0 line against the Bears in Week 12. Hockenson came into Sunday with just 76 receiving yards, so he could have trouble repeating the performance even if Jefferson misses another game, but Murray had success feeding the ball to Trey McBride last year with Arizona as well -- McBride posted a 29-275-1 line on 42 targets during the five games they were in the lineup together. Hockenson will look to keep rolling in a Week 5 road trip to New Orleans.

4360569_Jordan Mason_MIN.headline: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that Mason has a small fracture in his thumb that underwent surgery, and the running back will be placed on injured reserve, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
4360569_Jordan Mason_MIN.story: Mason emerged from the Vikings' Week 1 win against the Packers with a sore thumb, but the severity of the issue didn't become clear until O'Connell spoke to the media Wednesday. With Mason out for at least the next four games, Aaron Jones is set to lead the Vikings backfield for the foreseeable future, with Demond Claiborne, DeeJay Dallas and practice-squad member Jerome Ford all candidates for reps that don't go to Jones.

4426502_Drake London_ATL.headline: London played eight snaps on offense and didn't show up in the box score otherwise during the Falcons' 17-12 preseason win over the Dolphins on Friday.
4426502_Drake London_ATL.story: London was limited to playing the first quarter of Friday's exhibition game before observing the rest of the contest from the sidelines. Entering his fifth NFL season, the USC product has recorded at least 68 catches and 850 receiving yards in each of his four years with Atlanta. London has been one of the most productive receivers since entering the league in 2022, but his offensive output will be heavily tied to the production of the Falcons' starting quarterback, whether that's Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix (knee).

4361409_Jahan Dotson_ATL.headline: Dotson caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Friday's 17-12 preseason win over the Dolphins.
4361409_Jahan Dotson_ATL.story: Dotson accounted for three of Tua Tagovailoa's seven completions while Atlanta's starters were in the game, with three going to TE Kyle Pitts and one going to RB Brian Robinson. Offensive stars Bijan Robinson and Drake London sat out the preseason finale, but Dotson's involvement Friday suggests the 2022 first-round pick of the Commanders is positioned as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout behind London heading into the regular season.

3917914_Olamide Zaccheaus_ATL.headline: Zaccheaus enters training camp in a battle against Jahan Dotson and rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch for the Falcons' No. 2 wide receiver job behind Drake London (undisclosed), Tim Weaver of USA Today reports.
3917914_Olamide Zaccheaus_ATL.story: After stints in Philadelphia, Washington and Chicago, Zaccheaus opted to sign a one-year contract in March to rejoin the Falcons, with whom he previously played from 2019-22. The Virginia product has eclipsed 500 receiving yards just once in his NFL career, but given Atlanta's lack of reliable pass catchers behind London and tight end Kyle Pitts, Zaccheaus could establish himself as a consistent target for whoever is under center between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix (knee). Dotson brings four years of NFL experience to the table and little more production than Zaccheaus, but the journeyman's biggest competition figures to come from the rookie Branch, who made a strong impression on coaches with his speed, explosiveness and playmaking ability during college and in OTAs.

4360248_Kyle Pitts Sr._ATL.headline: Pitts caught all three of his targets for 59 yards in Friday's 17-12 preseason win over the Dolphins.
4360248_Kyle Pitts Sr._ATL.story: Pitts has shown excellent chemistry with QB Tua Tagovailoa during the preseason, accounting for 81 of Tagovailoa's 117 passing yards across parts of two preseason games. It remains to be seen whether Tagovailoa or Michael Penix (knee) will get the starting nod under center for Week 1 against the Steelers. Either way, Pitts is poised to maintain a prominent role on the heels of his 928-yard 2025 regular season.

4241479_Tua Tagovailoa_ATL.headline: The Falcons will have Tagovailoa start at quarterback in Sunday's season opener against the Steelers, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
4241479_Tua Tagovailoa_ATL.story: The Falcons were deciding between Tagovailoa and Michael Penix (knee) for the Week 1 starting assignment, and with the latter still getting back up to full speed as he works his way back from a torn ACL, Tagovailoa will get the nod. Tagovailoa likely won't have much leash as a starter, coming off a poor preseason in which he completed 10 of 13 pass attempts for 117 yards while fumbling twice (losing one).

4241474_Brian Robinson Jr._ATL.headline: The Athletic's Josh Kendall expects Robinson to have a goal-line role for the Falcons this season.
4241474_Brian Robinson Jr._ATL.story: "He has shown a physical style in practice that cements his role as the new Tyler Allgeier," Kendall wrote. "Bijan Robinson fantasy managers may not like how many goal-line carries he gets." Allgeier, of course, was a thorn in the side of Bijan's fantasy investors last season, out-carrying Atlanta's lead back 19 to 17 inside the 10-yard line while matching him with seven carries apiece inside the five-yard line. Allgeier also punched in four of those seven carries for touchdowns, while Bijan scored on just two of his chances. At 6-foot-1 and 225 pounds, the team's newest Robinson profiles similarly to Allgeier as a short-yardage, between-the-tackles type who can pick up tough yards. It sounds like the former Commander and 49er going to have some sort of role in those situations for the Falcons this season, which could mute Bijan's touchdown upside.

4360761_Michael Wilson_ARI.headline: Wilson caught seven of 13 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants.
4360761_Michael Wilson_ARI.story: The yardage and targets led the Cardinals on the afternoon, while his seven receptions tied Trey McBride for the team lead. Wilson has emerged as the clear No. 1 wideout for Jacoby Brissett, and he was the intended target on Deonte Banks' 98-yard pick-six that sealed the win for New York on the final play of the game. Wilson will take a 25-258-1 line on 44 targets through four games into a Week 5 tilt at home against the Lions.

4361307_Trey McBride_ARI.headline: McBride caught seven of 12 targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants.
4361307_Trey McBride_ARI.story: White the star tight end saw double-digit targets for a fourth straight game to begin the season, McBride couldn't turn the volume into meaningful production, with backup TE Elijah Higgins instead connecting with Jacoby Brissett on a two-yard score in the third quarter. McBride will carry a 33-242-2 line on a whopping 46 targets into a Week 5 clash at home with the Lions.

2578570_Jacoby Brissett_ARI.headline: Brissett completed 21 of 35 passes for 166 yards and two touchdowns with three interceptions in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants. He added 18 yards on four carries.
2578570_Jacoby Brissett_ARI.story: The veteran QB came into Sunday with only one turnover in the first three games of the year, but Brissett's three INTs killed any chance the Cardinals might have had of stealing a win at MetLife Stadium -- his third came on the final play of the game in the Giants' red zone, as his toss to Michael Wilson instead turned into a 98-yard pick-six by Deonte Banks. Brissett will take a 6:4 INT, and a three-game losing streak, into a Week 5 clash at home with the Lions.

4373626_Tyler Allgeier_ARI.headline: Allgeier rushed eight times for 42 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants. He added two catches for seven yards on two targets.
4373626_Tyler Allgeier_ARI.story: After Jeremiyah Love appeared to distance himself from Allgeier in Week 3 against the 49ers, Allgeier ended up out-snapping the rookie running back against the Giants. Love out-carried Allgeier 14 to eight Sunday, but it was Allgeier who found the end zone with a 22-yard score in the first quarter to give Arizona a 14-3 lead. Through four games, Allgeier has rushed 32 times for 112 yards and a touchdown, adding 10 catches for 35 yards on 10 targets. Splitting time with Love, Allgeier is touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks.

4431299_Rome Odunze_CHI.headline: Odunze caught six of seven targets for 94 yards in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets.
4431299_Rome Odunze_CHI.story: Odunze led the Bears in receiving yards while finishing two targets shy of Colston Loveland's team-high total as Tyson Bagent threw for 268 yards. This was the first time Odunze exceeded 52 receiving yards in a game this season, as he showed nice chemistry with the third QB to start a game for the Bears this season. Odunze's outlook is unlikely to change significantly whether the Bears get Caleb Williams (hamstring) back or stick with Bagent for Week 5 at Green Bay.

4685278_Luther Burden III_CHI.headline: Burden caught four of six targets for 63 yards and added an 11-yard rush in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets.
4685278_Luther Burden III_CHI.story: Burden finished second on the team in receiving yards, trailing Rome Odunze by 31. Both of Chicago's touchdowns came on the ground, but Tyson Bagent looked capable under center and threw for 268 yards. If Caleb Williams (hamstring) doesn't return in Week 5 against the Packers, Burden will likely continue to catch passes from Bagent. Burden has topped 60 yards in three of four games to begin his sophomore season, but he has yet to exceed 63 receiving yards in a game after reaching the 100-yard mark twice during his rookie campaign.

2973405_Kalif Raymond_CHI.headline: Raymond caught two passes for six yards and returned two punts for 16 yards during Chicago's win Sunday over the Jets.
2973405_Kalif Raymond_CHI.story: Raymond had a quiet outing just one week after leading the team with 90 receiving yards during the win over the Eagles. The 31-year-old has caught 21 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown across four games this season and should continue to serve as the Bears' No. 3 receiver behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden.

4431611_Caleb Williams_CHI.headline: Williams (hamstring) has made tangible progress in his recovery from a Grade 2 hamstring strain sustained in the Week 2 loss to the Vikings, Dan Wiederer of The Athletic reports.
4431611_Caleb Williams_CHI.story: Williams has yet to resume practicing with his teammates, but he has reportedly looked comfortable dropping back, planting and throwing the ball. Head coach Ben Johnson said Monday that Williams remains week-to-week and won't return to practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Packers, paving the way for Tyson Bagent to make a second consecutive start. Williams could be an option under center for the Bears as soon as Week 6 against the Falcons, though his return to game action would be precipitated by a successful return to practice without setbacks.

4608686_Kyle Monangai_CHI.headline: Monangai is tending to a turf toe injury that's making his status uncertain for the next 1-to-2 weeks, but the running back is aiming to play through it, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
4608686_Kyle Monangai_CHI.story: Monangai came out of Week 4 with a right thumb issue, but the health concern that popped up on Wednesday's practice report may be threatening his availability in the short term. He hasn't practiced so far this week and has only one more opportunity to mix into drills Friday before the Bears potentially make a ruling on him ahead of Sunday's game in Green Bay. If Monangai is inhibited or sidelined this weekend, D'Andre Swift (hip/knee) likely will handle a workhorse role out of Chicago's backfield, though Roschon Johnson also could experience an expanded workload.

4428331_Rashee Rice_KC.headline: Rice (hamstring) is believed to have sustained a "relatively minor" injury in Sunday's win over the Raiders and could be ready to play following the Chiefs' Week 5 bye, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
4428331_Rashee Rice_KC.story: Rice was forced from Sunday's game with a hamstring injury, but it appears Kansas City's upcoming bye could help him avoid missing any further action. Fellow wideout Tyquan Thornton (ankle) is sidelined indefinitely with an injury he himself picked up in Sunday's contest, so the Chiefs are heading into the off week with plenty of uncertainty in the wideout room. Xavier Worthy should remain busy regardless of who surrounds him, and Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen are next up -- at least for the time being -- to soak up leftover opportunities.

3139477_Patrick Mahomes_KC.headline: Mahomes completed 15 of 30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders. He also rushed twice for no gain.
3139477_Patrick Mahomes_KC.story: Mahomes threw touchdown passes of two yards and eight yards to Tyquan Thornton, who exited the game in the fourth quarter due to an ankle injury suffered at the end of a 55-yard catch. The Chiefs also lost Rashee Rice (hamstring) in the first half. Thornton is likely looking at a lengthy absence, but Rice has a chance to recover during Kansas City's Week 5 bye before facing the Chargers in Week 6. Mahomes has led the Chiefs to a 4-0 record while posting a 9:2 TD:INT, but the team is down to Xavier Worthy, Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals and Nikko Remigio at wide receiver at the moment.

4832955_Emmett Johnson_KC.headline: Johnson caught his lone target for 10 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
4832955_Emmett Johnson_KC.story: The rookie running back didn't handle a single rushing attempt behind Kenneth Walker's 22 carries for 177 yards and two touchdowns. Johnson still played 17 offensive snaps and remains the clear backup and bench stash to own in fantasy should something ever happen to Walker.

4685472_Tetairoa McMillan_CAR.headline: McMillan brought in five of 10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
4685472_Tetairoa McMillan_CAR.story: McMillan's yardage total comfortably paced the Panthers on the afternoon, and the second-year pro also led the team in targets while checking in as the runner-up in receptions. He's posted five catches apiece in each of his first two games of the season and parlayed them into a solid 176 receiving yards on 18 targets, all numbers that only serve to further cement his status as an integral component of Carolina's air attack. McMillan will next take aim at the Browns' inconsistent defense in a Week 3 road matchup next Sunday.

4695883_Jalen Coker_CAR.headline: Coker (ankle) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report.
4695883_Jalen Coker_CAR.story: After getting in a limited session Wednesday, Coker was unable to get any work one day later due to a lingering ankle issue. He was joined as a non-participant by fellow WR Xavier Legette (knee) on Thursday, leaving Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie as the other healthy options at the position behind No. 1 Tetairoa McMillan.

4430034_Xavier Legette_CAR.headline: Legette (knee) was listed as a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
4430034_Xavier Legette_CAR.story: Legette popped up on the injury report Thursday after practicing without limitations Wednesday. The 2024 first-round pick scored a 55-yard touchdown as part of a two-catch Week 2 performance against the Falcons after being held without a reception by the Bears in Week 1. Per Joe Person of The Athletic, Legette said Monday that he went for an MRI on his injury. Carolina is banged up at wide receiver behind Tetairoa McMillan, as Jalen Coker (ankle) was also sidelined Thursday.

4372780_Tommy Tremble_CAR.headline: Tremble caught three of his five targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 59-37 loss to the Bears.
4372780_Tommy Tremble_CAR.story: Tremble played 34 offensive snaps, which equated to just under 56 percent of the Panthers' total offensive plays. The tight end also contributed 11 special-teams snaps in the losing effort, showing some versatility in what was a productive offensive day for the Panthers overall.

4678008_Jonathon Brooks_CAR.headline: The Panthers placed Brooks (core) on injured reserve Wednesday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
4678008_Jonathon Brooks_CAR.story: As a result of the transaction, Brooks won't be eligible to play in any of the Panthers' next four games, but he's expected to miss additional time beyond that. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Wednesday that the running back will require surgery to repair a core muscle, which will keep him out for at least six weeks. With Brooks joining Trevor Etienne (ankle) on IR, AJ Dillon is left as the only reserve option on the 53-man roster behind lead back Chuba Hubbard. Carolina has Ahmani Marshall and Anthony Tyus on its practice squad, and the team will work out veteran Austin Ekeler on Wednesday and potentially sign him to bolster its running-back room, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston.

16737_Mike Evans_SF.headline: Evans (hip) didn't participate in Thursday's practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
16737_Mike Evans_SF.story: While Evans hasn't mixed into drills so far during Week 3 prep due to a hip issue, he was spotted running on a side field Thursday, per Matt Barrows of The Athletic. Evans is a rare player who doesn't need practice reps in order to be his normal self, or something close to it, on game days, but his status for Sunday's game versus the Cardinals could gain some clarity upon the 49ers posting its final injury report of the week Friday.

3126486_Deebo Samuel_SF.headline: Samuel caught three of four targets for 31 yards in the 49ers' 35-13 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He rushed one time for four yards.
3126486_Deebo Samuel_SF.story: Samuel didn't have quite the success he did in Week 1 against the Rams, but San Francisco controlled this game from start to finish, and Brock Purdy needed to attempt only 22 passes. With the Niners continuing to lose wideouts to injuries, Samuel is locked into the WR2 role behind Mike Evans (hip) headed into next Sunday's home date with the Cardinals. Through two games, Samuel has nine catches for 79 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets. He's also rushed two times for 16 yards.

4710714_De'Zhaun Stribling_SF.headline: The 49ers placed Stribling (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
4710714_De'Zhaun Stribling_SF.story: Stribling suffered what appeared to be a serious non-contact injury during the 49ers' Week 1 win against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia, but afterward tests revealed that his left Achilles was intact, and eventually he was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle. After undergoing surgery, he's expected to miss roughly 10 weeks, meaning a move to IR was inevitable. At least during the initial weeks of Stribling's absence, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and KhaDarel Hodge will handle WR duties for San Francisco.

3040151_George Kittle_SF.headline: Kittle caught all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
3040151_George Kittle_SF.story: Kittle gained half of his yardage on a 40-yard catch to start the second half, and he scored a 12-yard touchdown three plays later. He had just 12 receiving yards in the Week 1 win over the Rams, as Kittle returned from an Achilles tear sustained in January. Kittle will try to build on Sunday's strong performance in Week 3 against the Cardinals.

4696044_Kaelon Black_SF.headline: Black (groin) rushed seven times for 25 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
4696044_Kaelon Black_SF.story: Black suited up for his second NFL contest after being listed as questionable coming into the game. He actually had two more rushing yards than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey scored two touchdowns on 10 carries and added four catches for 43 yards. Black is poised to continue splitting the rushing workload with CMC in Week 3 against the Cardinals, though McCaffrey remains the preferred option in valuable goal-line and passing situations.

4241478_DeVonta Smith_PHI.headline: Smith (hamstring) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
4241478_DeVonta Smith_PHI.story: Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Smith was seen running on a side field Thursday, but the activity wasn't enough for him to be considered limited. It could be a sign that Smith is closing in on a return to practice, but until he does he may be trending toward a second straight absence Sunday at Jacksonville due to a hamstring issue. Friday's injury report may provide clarity on that front.

4870795_Makai Lemon_PHI.headline: Lemon caught three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
4870795_Makai Lemon_PHI.story: Lemon had a chance to step into a more prominent role on offense in the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), but he didn't really see an increase in production. The wide receiver's six targets are a new career high, but he now has registered three or fewer catches in all four games this season while never exceeding 30 receiving yards. Quarterback Jalen Hurts recorded only 93 total passing yards Sunday, so he'll have to be better for Lemon to see an increase in production in Week 5 versus Jacksonville.

3121023_Dallas Goedert_PHI.headline: Goedert (knee) was limited at practice Thursday.
3121023_Dallas Goedert_PHI.story: Goedert maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he looks to put a sprained MCL in his right knee further in the rearview mirror. Friday's practice report will reveal his odds to return to action Sunday in Jacksonville, but if he's inhibited or sidelined again this weekend, Johnny Mundt, E.J. Jenkins and practice-squad member Zach Ertz again will man tight end for the Eagles.

4040715_Jalen Hurts_PHI.headline: Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 93 yards and two touchdowns while rushing five times for 18 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
4040715_Jalen Hurts_PHI.story: Hurts threw second-quarter touchdowns of 18 and 10 yards to Darius Cooper, the first of which went off the hands of Rams defender Quentin Lake in the end zone. The Eagles started the game without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dallas Goedert (knee), lost Saquon Barkley (hamstring) in the first quarter and went a franchise-worst 0-for-12 on third down, yet they were still in position to win with a 10-point lead and the ball inside the Rams' 10-yard line halfway through the fourth quarter. Hurts failed on attempts to score with his legs and then his arm as that drive ended in a turnover on downs, and the Rams stormed back with two touchdown drives while the Eagles failed to pick up a first down on their final two drives. Hurts could struggle to produce again in Week 5 against the Jaguars in London if the Eagles remain without some of their key skill players.

4429013_Tank Bigsby_PHI.headline: The Eagles placed Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve Tuesday, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
4429013_Tank Bigsby_PHI.story: Bigsby will undergo core muscle surgery for an abdominal injury that he picked up during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. The fourth-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 9 against the Giants. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is also considered week-to-week, so with Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley could be the Eagles' starting running back for Week 5 against the Jaguars on Sunday in London.

3128429_Courtland Sutton_DEN.headline: Sutton secured three of four targets for 25 yards in the Broncos' 20-13 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
3128429_Courtland Sutton_DEN.story: Sutton saw Jaylen Waddle spearhead the Broncos' air attack with an eight-catch, 138-yard day on 10 targets, while the former posted his second straight underwhelming line to open the season. Sutton has seen a modest nine targets over his first two games, and it remains to be seen if Waddle is in the early stages of taking over the No. 1 role in the team's passing attack. Sutton will look to make more of an impact in a Week 3 home showdown against the Rams next Sunday night.

4431280_Troy Franklin_DEN.headline: Franklin caught one of two targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Jaguars.
4431280_Troy Franklin_DEN.story: With Marvin Mims (foot) inactive, Franklin played 13 of 62 offensive snaps as the clear No. 4 receiver behind Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant and Jaylen Waddle. Franklin's 27-yard grab was his lone catch of the season through two weeks. He'll need an injury to obtain any fantasy relevance in redraft formats.

3051876_Evan Engram_DEN.headline: Engram hauled in his lone target for 17 yards during the Broncos' 20-13 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
3051876_Evan Engram_DEN.story: Engram's five-yard catch early in the second quarter was nullified by an illegal formation penalty. The veteran tight end didn't show up in the box score until his 17-yard grab midway through the fourth quarter, which helped lead to a three-yard rushing touchdown by rookie Jonah Coleman three plays later. Engram was listed as a co-starter at tight end alongside Adam Trautman, with the former playing 32 of 62 offensive snaps (51.6 percent). Engram's offensive production figures to fluctuate on a week-to-week basis, especially with Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton commanding most of the targets from Bo Nix. The Broncos will welcome in the Rams for Week 3 on Sept. 27.

4568490_RJ Harvey_DEN.headline: Harvey (hamstring) was listed as a full participant on Thursday's injury report.
4568490_RJ Harvey_DEN.story: Harvey missed Week 2 with a hamstring injury, but he got in a limited practice Wednesday and a full session a day later, so he is set to return to action Sunday against the Rams. Fellow running back J.K. Dobbins (hip) also practiced fully while Jonah Coleman (ankle) missed a second straight day of work, so Harvey may only need to share the snaps with one running back in Week 3 rather than two.

4426515_Puka Nacua_LA.headline: Nacua (hip) caught nine of 12 targets for 125 yards and added a two-yard rushing touchdown in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles.
4426515_Puka Nacua_LA.story: Nacua looked spry in his return from a two-game absence due to a hip injury that was also termed groin soreness. He had just one catch in the first half but scored a two-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter. The star wide receiver came alive as a pass catcher in the second half as the Rams stormed back from a 10-point deficit with two unanswered fourth-quarter touchdowns. Nacua's injury appears to be in the rearview mirror heading into a Week 5 home game against the Bills.

4569382_Jordan Whittington_LA.headline: Whittington (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus Denver, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
4569382_Jordan Whittington_LA.story: Whittington wasn't available for Monday's 28-6 win over the Giants. He didn't practice Wednesday to begin the week. However, head coach Sean McVay indicated the wideout would be available in Week 3, so his full participation in Friday's practice and omission from the injury report isn't a surprise. With Puka Nacua (hip) doubtful, Whittington could be in line for a more prominent role alongside Davante Adams.

4242557_Colby Parkinson_LA.headline: Parkinson (shoulder/knee) is inactive for Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Eagles.
4242557_Colby Parkinson_LA.story: The veteran tight end took a questionable tag into the weekend after missing practice all week, and Parkinson's inactive status has now been confirmed. While he tends to his pair of injuries and targets a return for a Monday night, Oct. 12 home showdown with the Bills in Week 5, Parkinson's snaps and targets are expected to be absorbed by Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and rookie second-round pick Max Klare, the Rams' three remaining healthy tight ends with Terrance Ferguson (ankle, IR) also unavailable.

12483_Matthew Stafford_LA.headline: Stafford completed 32 of 51 passes for 317 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles. He also rushed three times for 10 yards.
12483_Matthew Stafford_LA.story: Stafford was picked off twice in the first half as the Rams took a 20-10 deficit into the locker room. The veteran QB didn't throw a touchdown pass in the return of top target Puka Nacua (hip) from a two-game absence, but Stafford led a pair of fourth-quarter touchdown drives culminating in Kyren Williams rushing scores as the Rams produced 14 unanswered points in the final four minutes to improve to 2-2. Stafford takes an underwhelming 6:6 TD:INT into a Week 5 home game against the Bills.

4429096_Blake Corum_LA.headline: Corum rushed five times for 14 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles. He added one catch for seven yards on two targets.
4429096_Blake Corum_LA.story: Kyren Williams has greatly outplayed Corum through the first four weeks of the season, and that continued against Philly, as Williams turned 16 carries into 80 yards and two touchdowns. He also caught 10 passes for 67 yards on 13 targets in the passing game. Williams ended up out-snapping Corum 70 to 13, leaving the latter as nothing more than a fantasy bench stash.

4682745_Jaylen Wright_MIA.headline: Wright (foot) showed up as a limited participant at Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
4682745_Jaylen Wright_MIA.story: Wright practiced without limitations Wednesday but took a step back Thursday. He missed Miami's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs due to a foot injury but returned in Week 4 against the Vikings. Wright was outplayed by Ollie Gordon against Minnesota, and Gordon is likely in line to get the majority of rushing opportunities Sunday against the Bengals, regardless of Wright's status.

4883647_Elic Ayomanor_TEN.headline: Ayomanor caught two of three targets for 69 yards during the Titans' 24-20 loss to the Eagles on Sunday.
4883647_Elic Ayomanor_TEN.story: Ayomanor doubled his catches Sunday compared to Week 1 against the Jets. He connected with Cam Ward on a 28-yard pass late in the second quarter that led to a 37-yard field goal by Joey Slye at the end of the first half. Ayomanor was then responsible for the game's longest play with a 41-yard catch in the fourth quarter, hurdling defensive back Marcus Epps in the process. Ayomanor played only 28 of 53 offensive snaps (52.8 percent), third-most among Titans wide receivers. However, his 69 receiving yards was a career high, and he's recorded at least 50 receiving yards in three of his last five regular-season games dating back to the 2025 campaign. The Titans will hit the road for Week 3 against the Giants on Sept. 27.

2576581_C.Moore_BAL.headline: Moore (ankle) was limited during Thursday's practice.
2576581_C.Moore_BAL.story: Moore was limited for a second consecutive day, so he may be heading toward an injury designation for Sunday's meeting with Dallas. The wideout logged 32 snaps in the 24-17 loss to New Orleans in Week 2, second behind Rashod Bateman (54), though he ended the day with just one catch (three targets) for six yards. Zay Flowers (ankle) could be in line for another absence in Week 3, and if Moore joins him on the shelf against Dallas, LaJohntay Wester and Devontez Walker may need to be more involved alongside Bateman.

4429795_Jahmyr Gibbs_DET.headline: Gibbs rushed 15 times for 46 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of seven targets for 31 yards in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
4429795_Jahmyr Gibbs_DET.story: Gibbs' season-low rushing yardage total was particularly surprising considering no team had allowed more rushing yards to running backs than Carolina coming into Week 4. Gibbs also wasn't able to make up for the lack of rushing production with his work as a pass catcher, but he at least added his fifth rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run late in the first half. Gibbs and the Lions will look to bounce back in a Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

4429160_De'Von Achane_MIA.headline: Achane rushed 20 times for 74 yards while catching three of six targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
4429160_De'Von Achane_MIA.story: Achane racked up 23 touches after touching the ball 11 times in Week 1, but the speedster has struggled to find running room while consistently facing stacked boxes. He is averaging a meager 3.5 yards per rushing attempt heading into a Week 3 home game against the Chiefs, which is a departure from Achane's excellent efficiency in previous seasons, as he averaged 5.7 yards per carry last season and has a career mark of 5.6 YPC. Defenses are daring Malik Willis and Miami's underwhelming wide-receiver room to beat them, and Miami's offense hasn't been up to the task during the team's 0-2 start.

4882093_Bhayshul Tuten_JAX.headline: Tuten rushed 17 times for 73 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
4882093_Bhayshul Tuten_JAX.story: Tuten filled his usual role as the clear lead option in Jacksonville's ground attack with aplomb, grinding out tough yards on many of his carries and also contributing a 20-yard run. He also recorded multiple receptions for the third consecutive game, and although he saw backfield mate Chris Rodriguez score the Jaguars' only rushing touchdown of the day that came on a breakaway run from 25 yards out as opposed to in close. Tuten has at least 15 carries in three of his first four games heading into a Week 5 showdown against the Eagles in London next Sunday.

4428718_Tre Tucker_LV.headline: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs.
4428718_Tre Tucker_LV.story: Tucker's eight targets tied Ashton Jeanty for third on the team behind Brock Bowers' 11 and Michael Mayer's 10 on a day Kirk Cousins attempted 52 passes. With Bowers back from a knee injury, Tucker has turned 12 targets into eight catches for 87 yards over the last two weeks with Bowers active. Tucker is a big-play threat but a boom-or-bust, low-floor fantasy bet most weeks.

4569603_Malik Washington_MIA.headline: Washington caught all five of his targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Vikings.
4569603_Malik Washington_MIA.story: The third-year wideout led the Dolphins in catches, yards and targets, but he didn't have much competition as Malik Willis attempted only 17 passes in total. Washington is still looking for his first TD of 2026, but he's become Willis' top downfield option, posting a 17-219-0 line on 28 targets through four games. Washington will try to build on this effort in a Week 5 home clash with the Bengals.

4249417_Jalen Tolbert_MIA.headline: Tolbert (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
4249417_Jalen Tolbert_MIA.story: Tolbert will continue to be a healthy scratch for the Dolphins as the team rides with its young talent at wide receiver. Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman will continue to suit up behind the primary option, Malik Washington.

4869645_Caleb Douglas_MIA.headline: Douglas (ankle) didn't practice Thursday, C. Isaiah Smalls of the Miami Herald reports.
4869645_Caleb Douglas_MIA.story: Douglas hasn't practiced or played since hurting his ankle in Week 2 against the 49ers. The rookie third-round pick is trending toward a third consecutive absence Sunday against the Bengals, though Douglas could gain at least a glimmer of hope to play by returning to practice Friday.

4367209_Greg Dulcich_MIA.headline: Dulcich played 20 offensive snaps but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during the Dolphins' 15-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
4367209_Greg Dulcich_MIA.story: Dulcich and Malik Willis connected on five of seven passes for 55 yards against the Chiefs in Week 3, but the duo failed to link up with each other during Sunday's loss. It was the first time since Week 8 of the 2025 season that Dulcich didn't record a target, and perhaps more notably, his 20 offensive snaps were behind rookie third-round tight end Will Kacmarek's 24. The Dolphins will head back to Miami to host the Bengals for Week 5.

4242512_Malik Willis_MIA.headline: Willis completed nine of 17 passes for 85 yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Vikings. He added 11 yards on two carries and lost a fumble.
4242512_Malik Willis_MIA.story: It was a miserable day for the Miami passing game against Brian Flores' defense, as Willis wasn't able to find receivers downfield -- his longest completion went for just 17 yards to Malik Washington -- or escape the pocket to do damage with his legs. Willis has produced just two TDs (one through the air, one on the ground) through four starts against four turnovers (two INTs and two lost fumbles) while completing just 56.3 percent of his passes, but there's been no suggestion the 0-4 Dolphins will make a switch at QB ahead of a Week 5 home tilt against the Bengals.

4382466_Jalen Nailor_LV.headline: Nailor (concussion) isn't practicing Thursday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
4382466_Jalen Nailor_LV.story: After sustaining a concussion in this past Sunday's loss to the Chiefs, Nailor hasn't made enough progress through the five-step protocol to resume taking any on-field reps. He'll have one more chance this week to practice in some capacity, but at this stage, Nailor looks to be trending toward sitting out this Sunday against New England.

4603186_Jack Bech_LV.headline: The Raiders placed Bech (forearm) on injured reserve Tuesday.
4603186_Jack Bech_LV.story: Bech will be sidelined for at least the Raiders' next four games after sustaining a fractured left forearm during Sunday's 35-27 win over the Saints. In a corresponding move, the Raiders signed Cody White off their practice squad. White, who already has three touchdowns this season, is the leading candidate to replace Bech as the No. 3 wideout behind Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor.

4432665_Brock Bowers_LV.headline: Bowers (knee) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice, Anthony Galaviz of The Fresno Bee reports.
4432665_Brock Bowers_LV.story: After opening Week 5 prep with a limited practice Wednesday, Bowers upgraded to full activity a day later, clearing up any concern about his status for Sunday's game at New England. Since making his season debut Week 3 after missing the Raiders' first two games while recovering from a meniscus trim, Bowers has functioned as the team's top pass catcher, leading the way in catches (16), receiving yards (202) and targets (25) by healthy margins while finding the end zone twice.

14880_Kirk Cousins_LV.headline: Cousins completed 31 of 52 passes for 365 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs. He also threw a successful two-point conversion.
14880_Kirk Cousins_LV.story: Cousins opened the scoring with a 27-yard touchdown pass to Ian Thomas in the first quarter, but his next touchdown pass didn't come until 1:46 remained in the fourth quarter, when Cousins connected with Brock Bowers for a 20-yard touchdown and added a two-point conversion to Cody White to cut the Raiders' deficit to three points. Vegas got the ball back, but Cousins was picked off on the game's penultimate play as the Raiders' comeback bid came up short. Despite Sunday's setback, Cousins has led the Raiders to a 3-1 record while posting an 11:4 TD:INT heading into a Week 5 road game against the Patriots.

4686658_Mike Washington Jr._LV.headline: Washington rushed nine times for 18 yards in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs. He added one catch for minus-1 yard on two targets.
4686658_Mike Washington Jr._LV.story: Washington's nine carries were his most in a single game to begin the season and came one week after he broke out for 54 yards and a touchdown on five carries against the Saints. The rookie running back closed the gap some on Ashton Jeanty atop the backfield, but Washington didn't do much with his chances against Kansas City. He remains one of the stronger fantasy bench stashes.

4697815_Rachaad White_WAS.headline: White (shoulder) was limited at practice Thursday.
4697815_Rachaad White_WAS.story: White was sidelined all of last week before missing this past Sunday's game versus the Colts in London while dealing with a shoulder injury. He maintained his activity level from Wednesday, as did fellow RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin). With the Commanders waiving rookie Kaytron Allen on Thursday, the team currently has just Croskey-Merritt, White and Austin Ekeler at the position on the active roster.

4426348_Jayden Daniels_WAS.headline: Offensive coordinator David Blough said Thursday that Daniels (left elbow) is "full go" for Sunday's game against the Giants and won't have any limitations, John Keim of ESPN.com reports.
4426348_Jayden Daniels_WAS.story: Daniels returned to practice Wednesday and participated without limitations after missing the previous two games due to a dislocated left elbow. According to Blough, the Commanders plan to have the entire playbook available for their mobile quarterback. If Daniels were to sustain any setbacks in his return, undrafted rookie Athan Kaliakmanis would likely be thrust back into action, as Marcus Mariota (knee) isn't expected to be available after spraining his knee in Washington's Week 4 loss to the Colts.

3121422_Terry McLaurin_WAS.headline: McLaurin (hamstring) officially didn't practice Thursday.
3121422_Terry McLaurin_WAS.story: McLaurin thus has just one more opportunity to mix into drills this week before the Commanders potentially make a call on his status ahead of Sunday's game versus the Giants. Both he and Stefon Diggs (hamstring) haven't practiced so far this week, meaning Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Luke McCaffrey are the current healthy wide receivers on Washington's active roster.

2976212_Stefon Diggs_WAS.headline: Diggs (hamstring) didn't participate in Thursday's practice.
2976212_Stefon Diggs_WAS.story: Though he didn't mix into drills, Diggs was present for the open portion of Thursday's practice and was seen working out off to the side under the supervision of trainers, per Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic. Washington also listed fellow receiver Terry McLaurin (hamstring) as a non-participant, giving him and Diggs just one more chance apiece to practice this week before the Commanders potentially make rulings on both players ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants. Currently, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Luke McCaffrey are the healthy options at the position on Washington's active roster.

5081432_Antonio Williams_WAS.headline: Williams caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts.
5081432_Antonio Williams_WAS.story: With Terry McLaurin (hamstring) inactive, Williams finished second to Stefon Diggs in targets, but the rookie wideout wasn't able to do much with the volume as Athan Kaliakmanis ended up having to make his NFL debut in relief of Marcus Mariota (knee) at quarterback. Williams has produced a 12-124-1 line on 19 targets through his first four games, and he'll be a volatile option in Week 5 against the Giants depending on whether Jayden Daniels (elbow) and McLaurin are able to return.

4360635_Chig Okonkwo_WAS.headline: Okonkwo (hamstring) remained limited at Thursday's practice.
4360635_Chig Okonkwo_WAS.story: Okonkwo is one of three prominent pass catchers dealing with hamstring injuries for the Commanders, along with wide receivers Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. While McLaurin and Diggs have both been unable to practice in any capacity, Okonkwo has put forth two limited sessions to begin Week 5 prep ahead of Sunday's game against the NFC East rival Giants.

4569987_Jaylen Warren_PIT.headline: Warren rushed 17 times for 93 yards and secured three of six targets for 33 yards in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
4569987_Jaylen Warren_PIT.story: Warren once again had near total control of the Steelers' ground attack, as Rico Dowdle (toe) missed a second consecutive contest. As he'd done in the Week 3 win over the Bengals, Warren capitalized on the opportunity to comfortably eclipse the century mark in total yards. Warren compiled 220 rushing yards and another 82 yards through the air over the last two games while serving as the unquestioned lead back, but if Dowdle is able to make it back for a Week 5 matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11, the former will see a hit to his touches.

2991662_Mack Hollins_NE.headline: Hollins (calf) wasn't spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice available to media, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
2991662_Mack Hollins_NE.story: Hollins appears to be missing a second consecutive practice ahead of Sunday's tilt against the Raiders. If Hollins is unable to suit up Sunday, Efton Chism could work alongside Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas in three-receiver, while Hollins' strong blocking may be missed in the running game.

4429086_Michael Mayer_LV.headline: Mayer caught eight of 10 targets for 82 yards in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs.
4429086_Michael Mayer_LV.story: Mayer led the Raiders in catches while finishing four receiving yards and one target shy of Brock Bowers' team-high totals. Kirk Cousins has relied heavily on his tight ends in the passing game, and even third-stringer Ian Thomas got in on the fun with a 27-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter. Bowers will continue to lead the position group in Week 5 against the Patriots, but Mayer remains an integral part of Vegas' offense as well.

3915411_Ty Johnson_BUF.headline: Johnson (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Alec White of the Bills' official site reports. "Ty Johnson will be good to go," coach Joe Brady said Friday.
3915411_Ty Johnson_BUF.story: He missed both of the first two games of the season, but with receivers DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (ankle) both being listed as questionable, Johnson's receiving skills out of the backfield might be useful for the offense. Johnson really isn't recommended for fantasy unless anything happens to starter James Cook, but the former's presence on the field does knock Ray Davis down a peg.

4240472_Noah Gray_KC.headline: Gray caught two of his three targets for 17 yards in the Chiefs' 30-27 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
4240472_Noah Gray_KC.story: Gray was utilized at a similar rate to No. 1 TE Travis Kelce in the contest. The tight end once again contributed to blocking for Kenneth Walker in 12-personnel packages but has not logged a lot of attention in the Chiefs' passing offense this season.

4379399_James Cook III_BUF.headline: Cook rushed 12 times for 75 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for eight yards in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
4379399_James Cook III_BUF.story: Cook consistently ripped off productive gains on the ground against the Patriots' defense, with his longest run of the day going for a relatively modest 17 yards. Cook's overall rushing opportunities were still somewhat capped, and he finished with a new season low in carries. However, the talented back extended his streak of games with a rushing TD to three when he went in from eight yards out early in the second quarter. Cook has now averaged well over 6.0 yards per carry for three straight games and is up to 421 rushing yards and three scores on the ground heading into a Week 5 road showdown against the Rams on Monday night, Oct. 12.

4035538_David Montgomery_HOU.headline: Montgomery carried the ball 10 times for 24 yards and added 19 receiving yards on a hook-and-ladder play in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
4035538_David Montgomery_HOU.story: The veteran RB's longest gain on the ground went for only six yards, and Woody Marks scampered for the Texans' only rushing TD of the afternoon on a six-yard run just before the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter -- a score set up by Montgomery's 19-yard dash following a lateral from Dalton Schultz just one play before. Montgomery hasn't found the end zone himself or reached 50 scrimmage yards since Week 1, a streak he'll look to end in a Week 5 road trip to Tennessee.

4596472_Jalon Daniels_TB.headline: Daniels completed 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions and rushed eight times for 55 yards in the Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
4596472_Jalon Daniels_TB.story: The undrafted rookie was thrust into his first NFL start much sooner than expected thanks to Baker Mayfield's thumb injury, and all told, Daniels acquitted himself reasonably well. He unsurprisingly had his share of struggles as a passer, and in addition to his pair of picks, he also took three sacks. Daniels' two turnovers did lead to 10 total points for the Packers, but the Kansas product also provided plenty of valuable production on the ground and fired his first career touchdown to Kenny Gainwell from 10 yards out to open the fourth quarter. Daniels won't get the benefit of another full week of practice before taking the field for his second start, however, as the Bucs pay a visit to the Cowboys for a Week 5 matchup Thursday night.

3051889_Laquon Treadwell_IND.headline: Treadwell caught five of six targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders.
3051889_Laquon Treadwell_IND.story: With Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve and Keenan Allen (groin) inactive for Week 4, Treadwell paced the Colts' wideouts with 56 offensive snaps and ran a team-high 36 routes on Daniel Jones' 37 dropbacks. Josh Downs and Ashton Dulin fell in line behind Treadwell in terms of playing time at the position. Treadwell has nine catches for 123 yards on 11 targets through four games.

4430802_Darnell Washington_PIT.headline: Washington caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in a loss to Cleveland on Thursday.
4430802_Darnell Washington_PIT.story: Washington was one of four Steelers who tied for second on the team with three receptions. Most of his yardage came on a 21-yard touchdown catch early in the fourth quarter that brought Pittsburgh to within five points. Washington began the campaign with a quiet first two weeks, but he's put together a solid 6-94-1 receiving line over his past two contests. He and the Steelers will next face Indianapolis at home next Sunday.

4887558_Emanuel Wilson_SEA.headline: Wilson racked up 21 carries for 81 yards and one touchdown and added three catches (on four targets) for 39 yards and another TD during Sunday's 30-23 win versus the Chargers.
4887558_Emanuel Wilson_SEA.story: In the wake of Jadarian Price's placement on injured reserve due to a chest issue, Wilson got the first chance to pace the Seahawks backfield, and he parlayed the second-highest touch count of his career into his second ever outing with 100-plus yards from scrimmage and his second two-TD performance. Meanwhile, fellow RB George Holani received eight touches, which he turned into 20 total yards. Until Zach Charbonnet (knee, reserve/PUP list) is able to return to action, Wilson figures to be Seattle's lead runner.

4575131_Jacory Croskey-Merritt_WAS.headline: Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a limited practice participant Thursday.
4575131_Jacory Croskey-Merritt_WAS.story: Croskey-Merritt maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he tends to a groin injury. Friday's practice report may provide clarity on his status ahead of Sunday's contest against the Giants. Through four games this season, Croskey-Merritt boasts 197 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD on 61 touches.

4595342_Oronde Gadsden_LAC.headline: Gadsden secured five of eight targets for 36 yards and recorded a two-yard carry during Sunday's 30-23 defeat in Seattle.
4595342_Oronde Gadsden_LAC.story: With position mates David Njoku (fibula) on IR and Charlie Kolar (forearm) sidelined the last two contests, Gadsden has had uneven results, posting a bagel on three targets in Week 3 at Buffalo before Sunday's season-best performance. Gadsden likely was helped this week by the early exit of No. 1 WR Ladd McConkey (foot), but the former's efficiency (9.5 YPC, 5.7 YPT) has been lacking in a floundering Chargers offense so far this season. In any case, for as long as Njoku and Kolar are out of the lineup, Gadsden shouldn't have a problem leading the team's TEs in most receiving categories.

4819231_Kaleb Johnson_GB.headline: Johnson logged eight carries for 42 yards and lost one fumble in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
4819231_Kaleb Johnson_GB.story: Johnson had a strong 5.3 yards per carry in the win but coughed up the football in a close game. The running back relinquished the ball to Tykee Smith with 9:13 remaining in the fourth quarter on the Tampa Bay 4-yard line while the Packers were up by only three points. The defense held off the Buccaneers offense, but it appears the Packers chose to ride MarShawn Lloyd to finish out the game.

4429022_Kayshon Boutte_HOU.headline: Boutte caught three of four targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
4429022_Kayshon Boutte_HOU.story: With Nico Collins back from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury, he dominated targets and left the remainder of the Houston pass catchers fighting for leftovers. Boutte ran 24 routes on C.J. Stroud's 35 dropbacks, but the summer trade pickup has yet to really make an impact with the Texans, recording nine catches for 115 yards on 13 targets after four games.

4890973_Ashton Jeanty_LV.headline: Jeanty was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice due to ankle and foot injuries, Anthony Galaviz of The Fresno Bee reports.
4890973_Ashton Jeanty_LV.story: The Raiders listed Jeanty with the ankle issue on their initial Week 5 injury report posted Wednesday, when the running back turned in a full practice. Not only did he take a step back in activity Thursday, but he's also nursing a foot injury in addition to the ankle concern. While the Raiders haven't yet indicated that Jeanty's availability for Sunday's game against the Patriots is in peril, fantasy managers will want to keep close tabs on his practice activity Friday.

4870808_Jeremiyah Love_ARI.headline: Love (ankle) stayed limited at Thursday's practice, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
4870808_Jeremiyah Love_ARI.story: Love emerged from a Week 4 loss at the Giants with a new ankle injury that's not related to the high-ankle sprain that he tended to in August. Friday's practice report will reveal whether or not he heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

4431545_Will Shipley_PHI.headline: Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams. He also returned three kickoffs for 65 yards.
4431545_Will Shipley_PHI.story: Shipley was the last man standing in Philadelphia's backfield after Saquon Barkley (hamstring) exited in the first quarter and Tank Bigsby (undisclosed) left in the fourth quarter. Bigsby had been working ahead of Shipley after Barkley's exit, but if neither of Philadelphia's top two running backs are available in Week 5, Shipley could take on the lead role against the Jaguars in London.

4241983_C.White_LV.headline: White (ankle) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Anthony Galaviz of The Fresno Bee reports.
4241983_C.White_LV.story: It's not clear when White picked up the injury, but that he got in some activity at practice Wednesday suggests it's probably not overly serious. As long as he can upgrade to full participation Thursday or Friday, there's a solid chance he'll be able to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

3916148_Tony Pollard_TEN.headline: Pollard (foot) was a full participant at Thursday's practice, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
3916148_Tony Pollard_TEN.story: Pollard has missed some practice time in recent weeks, including Wednesday's session, but he has been handling full workloads in games and is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game this season while having scored his first touchdown of the season in this past Sunday's loss to the Ravens. He's set to continue leading Tennessee's backfield Sunday against the Texans in a clash between winless AFC South teams.

4685702_Quinshon Judkins_CLE.headline: Judkins rushed 17 times for 53 yards and a touchdown and brought in six of seven targets for 43 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
4685702_Quinshon Judkins_CLE.story: Judkins was in his customary workhorse role in the Browns' ground attack, although as his final rushing line indicates, he found running room hard to come by on most of his carries. Even the second-year back's first rushing touchdown of the season didn't come easy, as Judkins had to power his way in from two yards out in the second quarter. However, he was able to find plenty of success as a receiver, finishing as the team leader in receptions and tying for runner-up status in targets with numbers that also qualified as new career-high figures. Judkins' backfield mates Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin combined for just three carries between them -- although the latter took his one tote for a 28-yard touchdown -- so Cleveland's clear lead back will continue to helm the run game in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

4695404_Isaiah Davis_NYJ.headline: Davis played just two offensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Bears.
4695404_Isaiah Davis_NYJ.story: With Breece Hall (thigh) inactive, Braelon Allen ended up playing 32 of 34 offensive snaps out of the backfield for the Jets, leaving no room for Davis. He can continue to be ignored in most fantasy formats.

2576980_Marcus Mariota_WAS.headline: Mariota (knee) will not be placed on injured reserve, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
2576980_Marcus Mariota_WAS.story: With Washington declining to place Mariota on injured reserve, the veteran quarterback appears set to avoid a long-term absence after aggravating his previously-injured knee in last Sunday's loss to the Colts. Jayden Daniels (elbow) is expected to start Sunday's game against the Giants.

4242335_Jonathan Taylor_IND.headline: Taylor carried the ball 20 times for 95 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders. He also caught one of four targets for two yards.
4242335_Jonathan Taylor_IND.story: Both scores came from five yards out in the second and third quarters, as the Colts went with a ground-heavy offense once Marcus Mariota (knee) was knocked out of the game in London, forcing the Commanders to turn to third-string QB Athan Kaliakmanis, a seventh-round rookie. Taylor has six rushing TDs through four games along with 422 scrimmage yards, and he figures to see a hefty workload again on the road in Week 5 against the Steelers.

4685512_Jadarian Price_SEA.headline: Price (chest) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
4685512_Jadarian Price_SEA.story: Price saw his practice participation during Week 4 prep decline due to a chest injury before he was ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Chargers. The injury is severe enough for the rookie first-rounder to go on IR, meaning Price will be forced to miss at least the next four games and won't be eligible to return until at least Week 8 against the Bears on Sunday, Nov. 2. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani will serve as the Seahawks' top running backs for Week 4 due to Price's absence, but Zach Charbonnet (knee) could also be in the mix for backfield duties as soon as Week 5 against the 49ers if he's activated from the reserve/PUP list.

4567048_Kenneth Walker III_KC.headline: Walker rushed 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns while catching his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
4567048_Kenneth Walker III_KC.story: Walker's two touchdowns came just 19 seconds apart in the fourth quarter, as he gave Kansas City the lead with a two-yard touchdown run and added a 22-yard touchdown run to create some breathing room after the Raiders fumbled the ensuing kickoff. The free-agent addition has paid immediate dividends for his new team, racking up 537 rushing yards and six total touchdowns through four games with the Chiefs. Walker has handled heavy workloads early in the season and will have a chance to rest up during a Week 5 bye before the 4-0 Chiefs host the Chargers in Week 6.
